Every topic is now explained in a normal teaching style: what it means, how to recognise it, how to use it, common mistakes, and examples. This is meant to be studied like a teacher is explaining it\227not memorised like a dictionary. Exam grounding: The supplied MAH-MBA/MMS-CET material contains Verbal Ability questions involving error identification and sentence correction/rephrasing. For example, its sample asks candidates to identify an erroneous part and separately asks them to choose the best rewriting of a sentence. n filecite n turn1file0 n L1-L8 n

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 2 1. Parts of Speech In normal English: Think of a sentence as a team. Every word has a job. A noun names something, a pronoun stands in for a noun, a verb tells us what happens or what something is, an adjective describes a noun, and an adverb gives extra information about an action or description. Prepositions show relationships, conjunctions join ideas, and interjections show sudden emotion. What to remember: \177 Noun = naming word. \177 Pronoun = replacement word. \177 Verb = action/state word. \177 Adjective = describes a noun. \177 Adverb = describes how/when/where/how much. \177 Preposition = relationship word. \177 Conjunction = joining word. \177 Interjection = sudden feeling word. Examples: 1. The student solved the problem. (noun) 2. She solved it. (pronoun) 3. She solved it. (verb) 4. It was a difficult problem. (adjective) 5. She solved it quickly . (adverb) 6. The book is on the table. (preposition) 7. Riya and Aman studied. (conjunction) 8. Wow! That was fast. (interjection) Common mistake / exam tip: Exam tip: Do not identify a word by memorising its appearance. Identify what job it is doing in that sentence. 2. Articles \227 A, An, The In normal English: Articles are tiny words, but they create many entrance-exam errors. A and an generally introduce one non-specific countable noun. The points to a particular or already-known noun. The choice between a and an depends on the sound at the beginning, not simply the first letter. What to remember: \177 Use a before a consonant sound: a university, a European. \177 Use an before a vowel sound: an hour, an MBA, an honest person. \177 Use the when the listener knows which thing you mean. \177 Do not automatically put an before every word beginning with a vowel letter. \177 General plural/uncountable statements often use no article. Examples: 1. She is a university student. 2. He waited for an hour. 3. Please close the door beside you. 4. He is an honest man.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 3 5. Books can change lives. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: a honest is wrong because honest begins with a vowel sound; an university is wrong because university begins with a /yu n / consonant sound. 3. Determiners In normal English: Determiners sit before nouns and give us information about which noun, how many, how much, or whose noun we mean. You can think of them as labels placed before a noun. What to remember: \177 this/that = one nearby/far item \177 these/those = plural nearby/far items \177 many/few = countable plural nouns \177 much/little = uncountable nouns \177 each/every = individual members of a group \177 some/any = amount/number without exact quantity Examples: 1. This question is easy. 2. There are many candidates. 3. We have little time. 4. Each student received a sheet. 5. Do you have any doubts? Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: say many students , but much time . Do not say much students or many time. 4. Nouns In normal English: A noun is the name of a person, place, object, idea, quality, activity, or group. Some nouns are easy to see\227book, college, teacher. Others are ideas\227honesty, freedom, success. What to remember: \177 Countable nouns can normally be counted: one book, two books. \177 Uncountable nouns are treated as masses/ideas: information, advice, furniture. \177 Collective nouns name groups: team, committee, family. \177 Possessive nouns show ownership: student's book, students' books. \177 Plural nouns normally need correct plural spelling. Examples: 1. The teacher explained the rule. 2. Mumbai is a busy city . 3. Honesty builds trust. 4. The team celebrated. 5. I need some information . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: informations, advices, furnitures are not standard forms. Say information, advice, furniture . 5. Pronouns

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 4 In normal English: Pronouns are words that replace nouns so we do not repeat the same name again and again. Instead of saying 'Riya opened Riya's book because Riya needed Riya's notes', we say 'Riya opened her book because she needed her notes.' What to remember: \177 Subject: I, he, she, we, they \177 Object: me, him, her, us, them \177 Possessive: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs \177 Reflexive: myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves \177 Relative: who, whom, whose, which, that Examples: 1. She completed the work. 2. The teacher praised him . 3. This notebook is mine . 4. He prepared the presentation himself . 5. The student who won smiled. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: Rahul and me went is wrong in formal grammar; use Rahul and I went . But The teacher called Rahul and me is correct because it is an object. 6. Adjectives In normal English: An adjective describes or gives information about a noun or pronoun. Ask 'What kind?', 'Which one?', or 'How many?' to find many adjectives. What to remember: \177 Quality: difficult, beautiful, honest \177 Quantity/number: five, several, many \177 Demonstrative: this, that, these, those when used before nouns \177 Possessive: my, your, their \177 Participial adjectives: boring, bored, broken, interested Examples: 1. She gave a clear explanation. 2. They rented a large hall. 3. He solved five questions. 4. It was an interesting lecture. 5. The broken chair was replaced. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: I am boring means you cause boredom. I am bored means you feel boredom. 7. Degrees of Comparison In normal English: When one thing is described, use the positive form. When two things are compared, use the comparative form. When one is compared with a whole group of three or more, use the superlative form. What to remember: \177 Short adjectives often use -er/-est: tall, taller, tallest. \177 Longer adjectives often use more/most: useful, more useful, most useful.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 5 \177 Irregular: good/better/best; bad/worse/worst. \177 Do not use two comparative markers together. \177 Use 'than' with a comparative in normal comparisons. Examples: 1. This book is useful . 2. This book is more useful than that one. 3. This is the most useful book here. 4. Today is better than yesterday. 5. That was the worst mistake. Common mistake / exam tip: Common traps: more better , most best , more taller . Use only one comparison structure. 8. Adverbs In normal English: An adverb gives extra information about a verb, adjective, another adverb, or sometimes the whole sentence. Ask 'How?', 'When?', 'Where?', or 'How often?'. What to remember: \177 How: quickly, carefully, clearly \177 When: today, yesterday, soon \177 Where: here, outside, everywhere \177 Frequency: always, often, rarely, never \177 Degree: very, quite, extremely Examples: 1. She spoke clearly . 2. We will leave tomorrow . 3. Please wait outside . 4. He often practises. 5. The question was very difficult. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: She sings beautiful is wrong in standard grammar; She sings beautifully is correct because the word describes how she sings. 9. Verbs In normal English: A verb is the engine of a sentence. It tells us what happens, what someone does, or what state something is in. A sentence normally needs a verb to express a complete action/state. What to remember: \177 Main verb: study, run, know \177 Helping verb: is, are, has, do \177 Modal: can, should, must \177 Transitive verbs can take an object: open the door. \177 Intransitive verbs do not need a direct object: sleep, arrive. Examples: 1. They solved the puzzle. 2. She knows the answer.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 6 3. He is studying. 4. You should revise. 5. The train arrived . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: after a modal, use the base verb: can go , not can goes; should study , not should studied. 10. Tenses \227 Complete Picture In normal English: Tense tells us when an action happens and sometimes whether it is ongoing or completed. The easiest way to learn tenses is to attach each form to a timeline. What to remember: \177 Present simple: habit/fact \227 I study. \177 Present continuous: happening now \227 I am studying. \177 Present perfect: past action connected to now \227 I have studied. \177 Past simple: finished past \227 I studied yesterday. \177 Past continuous: action in progress in past \227 I was studying. \177 Past perfect: earlier of two past actions \227 I had studied before the test. \177 Future simple: later action \227 I will study. \177 Future continuous: action in progress later \227 I will be studying. Examples: 1. She studies every day. 2. She is studying now. 3. She has finished the chapter. 4. She studied yesterday. 5. She had finished before dinner. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: words like yesterday normally signal simple past. 'Since/for' often require a perfect construction when an action continues to the present. 11. Subject\226Verb Agreement In normal English: The subject is the person/thing doing or being something. The verb must agree with that subject. The biggest exam trap is a plural-looking word sitting near a singular subject. What to remember: \177 Each/every/neither/either normally take singular verbs. \177 A phrase between subject and verb does not change the subject. \177 Two subjects joined by and usually take a plural verb. \177 With either/or and neither/nor, the nearer subject often controls agreement in formal usage. \177 News, mathematics and some other nouns can look plural but take singular verbs depending on usage. Examples: 1. The student is ready. 2. The students are ready. 3. Each of the players has a jersey. 4. The box of books is heavy.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 7 5. Riya and Aman are ready. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: The list of topics are is wrong; the subject is list, so use is . 12. Prepositions In normal English: Prepositions are small words that show relationships. They can tell us where something is, when something happens, or how two ideas are connected. What to remember: \177 Place: in, on, under, beside \177 Time: at 6, on Monday, in June \177 Direction: to, towards, into, through \177 Common combinations must often be memorised. \177 Preposition + gerund is common: interested in learning. Examples: 1. The keys are on the table. 2. Class starts at 9. 3. She walked towards the gate. 4. He is interested in finance. 5. Success depends on practice. Common mistake / exam tip: Common traps: good at , interested in , capable of , responsible for , depend on . 13. Conjunctions In normal English: Conjunctions connect ideas. They help us show addition, contrast, choice, reason, condition, time, and more. What to remember: \177 and = addition \177 but/yet = contrast \177 or = choice \177 because = reason \177 although = contrast despite a condition \177 either...or / neither...nor / not only...but also = paired conjunctions Examples: 1. Riya and Aman prepared. 2. He was tired, but he continued. 3. Study now or revise later. 4. She stayed home because it rained. 5. Although it was late, they continued. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: avoid incorrect pairs such as although...but in standard exam constructions. 14. Phrases and Clauses In normal English: A phrase is a group of words that does not contain a complete subject-and-verb idea. A clause contains a subject and a verb. An independent clause can stand alone; a dependent clause needs another clause.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 8 What to remember: \177 Noun phrase: the new student \177 Prepositional phrase: in the classroom \177 Independent clause: She smiled. \177 Dependent clause: because she was happy \177 Relative clause: who won the prize Examples: 1. The girl in the blue dress smiled. 2. She smiled. 3. Because she was happy , she smiled. 4. The book that you gave me is useful. 5. We left when the rain stopped . Common mistake / exam tip: Exam use: recognising clauses helps you detect sentence fragments, comma-related structure errors and incorrect sentence combinations. 15. Modals In normal English: Modals show ability, possibility, permission, advice, obligation or prediction. They are followed by the base form of the verb. What to remember: \177 can/could = ability or possibility \177 may/might = permission or possibility \177 should/ought to = advice \177 must/have to = necessity \177 would = conditional/polite/request contexts Examples: 1. She can solve it. 2. You should revise . 3. You may leave . 4. Candidates must carry ID. 5. It might rain . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: He can goes is wrong. Say He can go . 16. Conditionals In normal English: Conditionals are 'if' situations. The tense pattern tells us whether we are talking about a general truth, a realistic future possibility, an unlikely situation, or an unreal past situation. What to remember: \177 Zero: If + present, present. \177 First: If + present, will + base. \177 Second: If + past, would + base. \177 Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3. \177 Do not normally put 'will' immediately after if in the basic first conditional.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 9 Examples: 1. If you heat ice, it melts . 2. If she studies, she will improve . 3. If I had time, I would practise . 4. If he had prepared, he would have succeeded . 5. If I were you, I would revise . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: If she will study, she will pass is normally wrong for the standard first conditional; use If she studies, she will pass . 17. Active and Passive Voice In normal English: In active voice, the subject does the action. In passive voice, the receiver of the action becomes the focus. The passive normally uses a form of 'be' plus the past participle. What to remember: \177 Present: is/am/are + V3 \177 Past: was/were + V3 \177 Future: will be + V3 \177 Modal: must/can/should be + V3 \177 Only transitive verbs normally form a normal passive with a direct object. Examples: 1. They solve the problem \256 The problem is solved . 2. She wrote the letter \256 The letter was written . 3. They will announce the result \256 It will be announced . 4. You must complete the form \256 It must be completed . 5. Someone stole the phone \256 The phone was stolen . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: do not change the tense while changing voice. 18. Direct and Indirect Speech In normal English: Direct speech repeats the speaker's exact words. Indirect speech reports the meaning. When reporting past speech, tenses often move one step back, but not every situation requires mechanical backshift. What to remember: \177 Statement: said that... \177 Yes/no question: asked whether/if... \177 Wh-question: asked + wh-word + statement order \177 Command: told/ordered + object + to + verb \177 Request: asked + object + to + verb Examples: 1. \223I am ready.\224 \256 She said she was ready . 2. \223I finished.\224 \256 He said he had finished . 3. \223Are you ready?\224 \256 He asked whether I was ready . 4. \223Where do you live?\224 \256 She asked where I lived . 5. \223Open the door.\224 \256 He ordered me to open it.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 10 Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: indirect questions use statement word order: 'He asked where I lived', not 'where did I live'. 19. Gerunds In normal English: A gerund is an -ing form that behaves like a noun. It can be the subject or object of a sentence and commonly follows certain verbs and prepositions. What to remember: \177 After enjoy: enjoy reading \177 After avoid: avoid making \177 After finish: finish studying \177 After preposition: interested in learning \177 As subject: Reading helps. Examples: 1. Reading improves vocabulary. 2. She enjoys reading . 3. They avoided arguing . 4. He is interested in learning . 5. Practising daily improves speed. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: enjoy to read is normally wrong; use enjoy reading . 20. Infinitives In normal English: The full infinitive is usually 'to + base verb'. It can express purpose, intention, a noun-like idea, or describe a noun. Some structures use a bare infinitive without 'to'. What to remember: \177 Purpose: to improve \177 After want/decide/hope/plan: to study \177 After certain verbs such as let/make: bare infinitive \177 After modal verbs: bare infinitive \177 Adjective-like: a book to read Examples: 1. She studied to improve . 2. He decided to practise . 3. To learn takes patience. 4. Let him go . 5. I have a book to read . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: He made me to go is wrong in standard usage; say He made me go . 21. Participles In normal English: Participles are verb forms used inside verb phrases or as adjectives. Present participles often end in -ing; past participles are commonly V3 forms. What to remember:

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 11 \177 Present participle: running water \177 Past participle: broken glass \177 Perfect participle: having finished \177 Continuous verb: is studying \177 Passive verb: was written Examples: 1. The shining stars looked beautiful. 2. The broken window was repaired. 3. Having finished the work, she left. 4. They are preparing . 5. The answer was written carefully. Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: avoid dangling modifiers. In 'Walking to college, the rain started', the rain appears to be walking. 22. Question Tags In normal English: A question tag is a short question added to the end of a statement. A positive statement normally takes a negative tag; a negative statement takes a positive tag. What to remember: \177 Use the same auxiliary/modal. \177 Use a matching pronoun. \177 If there is no auxiliary in simple present/past, use do/does/did. \177 Special cases such as 'Let's...' and imperatives have their own common patterns. \177 Intonation can change whether it is a real question, but the grammar pattern remains. Examples: 1. She is ready, isn't she? 2. He isn't late, is he? 3. You can swim, can't you? 4. They finished, didn't they? 5. Open the window, will you? Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: She likes tea, isn't she? is wrong; use doesn't she? because the main verb is likes. 23. Parallelism In normal English: Parallelism means that items in the same grammatical list should have the same shape. It makes sentences balanced and is a favourite source of correction questions. What to remember: \177 gerund + gerund + gerund \177 to-infinitive + to-infinitive + to-infinitive \177 noun + noun + noun \177 adjective + adjective + adjective \177 Keep paired conjunction structures balanced.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 12 Examples: 1. She likes reading, writing and travelling . 2. He wants to learn, to practise and to improve . 3. She is smart, disciplined and patient . 4. The job requires skill, patience and focus . 5. It is not only difficult but also time-consuming . Common mistake / exam tip: Common trap: reading, writing and to travel mixes forms. Use reading, writing and travelling . 24. Commonly Confused Words In normal English: These words cause errors because they look or sound similar. Learn their meaning and use them in sentences rather than memorising spelling alone. What to remember: \177 its = possession; it's = it is/it has \177 their = possession; there = place; they're = they are \177 your = possession; you're = you are \177 affect = usually verb; effect = usually noun \177 principal = head/person or main; principle = rule/belief Examples: 1. It's raining; the company changed its policy. 2. They're waiting there with their books. 3. You're responsible for your work. 4. Sleep can affect focus; the effect was clear. 5. The principal explained the school's principle . Common mistake / exam tip: Exam tip: expand contractions. If 'it's' means 'it is', it is correct; if you need possession, use 'its'.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 13 25. ERROR SPOTTING \227 HOW TO SOLVE IT ELI5: You are given a sentence split into parts. One part may contain a grammar error. Your job is not to rewrite the whole sentence immediately. First locate the broken rule. Use this checking order: 1) subject + verb, 2) pronoun, 3) article/determiner, 4) tense, 5) preposition, 6) adjective/adverb, 7) comparison, 8) parallelism, 9) word meaning. Example 1: Each of the students / have submitted / their assignment / on time. Explanation: Part 2: have \256 has . 'Each' is singular. Example 2: The list of topics / are / on the desk / near the window. Explanation: Part 2: are \256 is . The subject is 'list'. Example 3: She / is one of the best student / in the class / this year. Explanation: Part 2: student \256 students . One of the + plural noun. Example 4: The teacher asked / Rahul and I / to wait / outside. Explanation: Part 2: I \256 me . The pronoun is an object of 'asked'. Example 5: She completed the assignment / quick / and submitted it / before lunch. Explanation: Part 2: quick \256 quickly . It modifies 'completed'. Example 6: He is good / in mathematics / but weak / in English. Explanation: Part 2: in \256 at . Standard combination is good at. Example 7: He has completed / the work / yesterday / without help. Explanation: Part 3 creates a tense mismatch. Use simple past: 'He completed the work yesterday.' Example 8: The students / was waiting / outside the hall / for an hour. Explanation: Part 2: was \256 were . Students is plural. Source connection: The supplied MAH-MBA/MMS-CET material uses exactly this kind of four-part sentence and asks candidates to identify the erroneous part or choose 'No error'. n filecite n turn1file0 n L1-L8 n

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 14 26. CHOOSE THE CORRECT SENTENCE / SENTENCE IMPROVEMENT ELI5: Here the sentence may already look almost correct. Several options give different versions. Your job is to choose the version that follows standard grammar and gives the clearest meaning. Step-by-step: First understand the meaning. Then compare the subject and verb. Then check tense, pronouns, articles, prepositions, word order and unnecessary words. Example 1 A) She is a honest student. B) She is an honest student. C) She is honest a student. D) She is an honesty student. Why: B . Honest begins with a vowel sound, so use an. Example 2 A) Neither of the boys are ready. B) Neither of the boys is ready. C) Neither boys is ready. D) Neither of boys are ready. Why: B . Neither is singular in this construction. Example 3 A) He has went home. B) He has gone home. C) He had go home. D) He has going home. Why: B . Has + past participle; gone is V3. Example 4 A) I prefer tea than coffee. B) I prefer tea to coffee. C) I prefer tea from coffee. D) I prefer tea over than coffee. Why: B . The standard construction is prefer X to Y. Example 5 A) The news are surprising. B) The news is surprising. C) The news were surprising. D) The news have surprising. Why: B . News is normally treated as singular. Example 6 A) She is capable to solve it. B) She is capable of solving it. C) She is capable for solve it. D) She is capable solving it. Why: B . Capable of + gerund. Example 7 A) One of my friend is preparing. B) One of my friends is preparing. C) One of my friends are preparing. D) One of my friend are preparing. Why: B . One of + plural noun, followed by singular verb.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed English Grammar Guide Page 15 Example 8 A) She suggested me to study. B) She suggested that I study. C) She suggested me studying. D) She suggested to me study. Why: B is the standard formal construction.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 2 1. Parts of Speech Simple Hinglish explanation: Sentence ko ek team samjho. Har word ka ek kaam hota hai. Noun kisi person/place/thing/idea ka naam hota hai. Pronoun noun ki jagah aata hai. Verb action ya state batata hai. Adjective noun ko describe karta hai. Adverb action ke baare mein extra information deta hai. Preposition relationship batata hai, conjunction words/ideas ko join karta hai aur interjection sudden feeling dikhata hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Noun = naam wala word. \177 Pronoun = noun ki jagah. \177 Verb = action/state. \177 Adjective = noun ki quality/description. \177 Adverb = kaise, kab, kahan, kitni baar. \177 Preposition = relation. \177 Conjunction = joining word. \177 Interjection = sudden emotion. Examples: 1. The student solved the problem. \227 noun 2. She solved it. \227 pronoun 3. She solved it. \227 verb 4. It was a difficult problem. \227 adjective 5. She solved it quickly . \227 adverb Common mistake / exam tip: Exam trick: Word ko dekhkar nahi, sentence mein uska kaam dekhkar part of speech identify karo. 2. Articles \227 A, An, The Simple Hinglish explanation: Articles chhote words hain, lekin grammar mein bahut important hain. A aur an generally ek non-specific singular countable noun ke saath aate hain. The tab use hota hai jab particular/specific cheez ki baat ho. A ya an choose karte waqt spelling nahi, sound dekho. Yaad rakhna: \177 Consonant sound se pehle a : a university. \177 Vowel sound se pehle an : an hour. \177 Specific cheez ke liye the . \177 'u' letter hone ka matlab automatically a nahi; sound matter karta hai. \177 General plural nouns ke saath article zaroori nahi hota. Examples: 1. She is a university student. 2. He waited for an hour. 3. Close the door beside you. 4. He is an honest man. 5. Books can change lives. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: a honest n \256 an honest n ; an university n \256 a university n .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 3 3. Determiners Simple Hinglish explanation: Determiners noun se pehle aakar batate hain ki kaunsa noun, kitne nouns, kitni quantity ya kiski cheez hai. Basically noun ke pehle ek label ki tarah kaam karte hain. Yaad rakhna: \177 this/that = singular \177 these/those = plural \177 many/few = countable nouns \177 much/little = uncountable nouns \177 each/every = individual members \177 some/any = unspecified quantity/number Examples: 1. This question is easy. 2. There are many candidates. 3. We have little time. 4. Each student received a sheet. 5. Do you have any doubts? Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: many students n , much time n ; much students n , many time n . 4. Nouns Simple Hinglish explanation: Noun kisi person, place, object, idea, quality ya group ka naam hota hai. Kuch nouns physical hote hain jaise book aur teacher; kuch ideas hote hain jaise honesty aur success. Yaad rakhna: \177 Countable: one book, two books. \177 Uncountable: information, advice, furniture. \177 Collective: team, committee, family. \177 Possessive: student's book, students' books. \177 Plural form bhi correct honi chahiye. Examples: 1. The teacher explained the rule. 2. Mumbai is a busy city . 3. Honesty builds trust. 4. The team celebrated. 5. I need some information . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: informations/advice(s)/furnitures n . Standard forms: information, advice, furniture. 5. Pronouns Simple Hinglish explanation: Pronoun noun ko baar-baar repeat karne se bachata hai. 'Riya opened Riya's book because Riya needed Riya's notes' ki jagah hum bolte hain: 'Riya opened her book because she needed her notes.' Yaad rakhna: \177 Subject: I, he, she, we, they.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 4 \177 Object: me, him, her, us, them. \177 Possessive: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. \177 Reflexive: myself, yourself, himself, herself. \177 Relative: who, whom, whose, which, that. Examples: 1. She completed the work. 2. The teacher praised him . 3. This notebook is mine . 4. He prepared it himself . 5. The student who won smiled. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Rahul and me went n \256 Rahul and I went n . But 'The teacher called Rahul and me' is correct. 6. Adjectives Simple Hinglish explanation: Adjective noun ya pronoun ko describe karta hai. Simple test: 'Kaisa?', 'Kaunsa?', 'Kitne?' poochho. Jo answer milta hai, woh often adjective hota hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Quality: difficult, beautiful, honest. \177 Number/quantity: five, several. \177 Demonstrative: this, that, these, those. \177 Possessive: my, your, their. \177 Participial: boring, bored, broken, interested. Examples: 1. A clear explanation. 2. A large hall. 3. Five questions. 4. An interesting lecture. 5. The broken chair. Common mistake / exam tip: Important: I am boring = main doosron ko bore karta hoon. I am bored = mujhe boredom feel ho raha hai. 7. Degrees of Comparison Simple Hinglish explanation: Ek cheez ko describe karna positive hai. Do cheezon ko compare karna comparative hai. Teen ya zyada mein sabse zyada/least batana superlative hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 tall \256 taller \256 tallest \177 useful \256 more useful \256 most useful \177 good \256 better \256 best \177 bad \256 worse \256 worst \177 Comparative ke saath normally than aata hai. Examples:

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 5 1. This book is useful . 2. This book is more useful than that one. 3. This is the most useful book. 4. Today is better than yesterday. 5. That was the worst mistake. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: more better n , most best n , more taller n . Double comparison mat karo. 8. Adverbs Simple Hinglish explanation: Adverb verb, adjective ya another adverb ke baare mein extra information deta hai. Questions: How? When? Where? How often? Yaad rakhna: \177 How: quickly, carefully, clearly. \177 When: today, yesterday, soon. \177 Where: here, outside, everywhere. \177 Frequency: always, often, rarely, never. \177 Degree: very, quite, extremely. Examples: 1. She spoke clearly . 2. We leave tomorrow . 3. Wait outside . 4. He often practises. 5. Very difficult. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: She sings beautiful n \256 She sings beautifully n , because word 'sings' ko describe kar raha hai. 9. Verbs Simple Hinglish explanation: Verb sentence ka engine hai. Ye batata hai ki koi action kya ho raha hai ya koi state kya hai. Sentence ka meaning complete karne ke liye verb bahut important hota hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Main verb: study, run, know. \177 Helping verb: is, are, has, do. \177 Modal: can, should, must. \177 Transitive: open the door. \177 Intransitive: arrive, sleep. Examples: 1. They solved the puzzle. 2. She knows the answer. 3. He is studying. 4. You should revise. 5. The train arrived . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Modal ke baad base verb: can go n , can goes n ; should study n , should studied n .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 6 10. Tenses Simple Hinglish explanation: Tense basically batata hai action kab hua aur kya woh ongoing tha ya complete ho chuka tha. Tenses ko timeline ke through samjho. Yaad rakhna: \177 Present simple = habit/fact. \177 Present continuous = abhi chal raha hai. \177 Present perfect = past action ka present se connection. \177 Past simple = finished past. \177 Past continuous = past mein action chal raha tha. \177 Past perfect = past ke do actions mein jo pehle hua. \177 Future simple = future action. \177 Future continuous = future mein action ongoing hoga. Examples: 1. She studies every day. 2. She is studying now. 3. She has finished the chapter. 4. She studied yesterday. 5. She had finished before dinner. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: yesterday jaise time markers simple past ka strong clue hain. Since/for ke saath continuing action mein perfect forms common hain. 11. Subject\226Verb Agreement Simple Hinglish explanation: Subject ka verb ke saath match hona zaroori hai. Sabse common trap ye hai ki subject aur verb ke beech extra words aa jaate hain aur student nearest noun dekhkar galat verb choose kar leta hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Each/every/neither/either normally singular verb lete hain. \177 Subject aur verb ke beech phrase ho sakta hai; us phrase se agreement change nahi hota. \177 A and B usually plural verb lete hain. \177 Either/or aur neither/nor mein formal usage mein nearer subject agreement affect kar sakta hai. \177 News jaise words form mein plural lag sakte hain but normally singular verb lete hain. Examples: 1. The student is ready. 2. The students are ready. 3. Each player has a jersey. 4. The box of books is heavy. 5. Riya and Aman are ready. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: The list of topics are n . Subject 'list' hai \256 The list of topics is n . 12. Prepositions Simple Hinglish explanation: Preposition place, time, direction ya relationship batata hai. In words ko kai baar rule se zyada fixed combination ke saath yaad karna padta hai.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 7 Yaad rakhna: \177 Place: in, on, under, beside. \177 Time: at 6, on Monday, in June. \177 Direction: to, towards, into, through. \177 Common combinations memorise karo. \177 Preposition ke baad gerund aa sakta hai: interested in learning. Examples: 1. Keys are on the table. 2. Class starts at 9. 3. She walked towards the gate. 4. He is interested in finance. 5. Success depends on practice. Common mistake / exam tip: Important combinations: good at, interested in, capable of, responsible for, depend on. 13. Conjunctions Simple Hinglish explanation: Conjunctions ideas ko connect karte hain. Ye addition, contrast, choice, reason, condition etc. show karte hain. Yaad rakhna: \177 and = addition \177 but/yet = contrast \177 or = choice \177 because = reason \177 although = contrast \177 either...or / neither...nor / not only...but also = paired conjunctions Examples: 1. Riya and Aman prepared. 2. He was tired, but he continued. 3. Study now or revise later. 4. She stayed home because it rained. 5. Although it was late, they continued. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Standard exam sentence mein although...but jaise incorrect combinations se bachna hai. 14. Phrases and Clauses Simple Hinglish explanation: Phrase words ka group hai jo complete subject-verb idea nahi deta. Clause mein subject + verb hota hai. Independent clause akela complete sentence ban sakta hai; dependent clause ko support chahiye. Yaad rakhna: \177 Noun phrase: the new student. \177 Prepositional phrase: in the classroom. \177 Independent clause: She smiled. \177 Dependent clause: because she was happy.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 8 \177 Relative clause: who won the prize. Examples: 1. The girl in the blue dress smiled. 2. She smiled. 3. Because she was happy , she smiled. 4. The book that you gave me is useful. 5. We left when the rain stopped . Common mistake / exam tip: Exam use: Isse sentence fragments aur clause-related errors identify karna easier hota hai. 15. Modals Simple Hinglish explanation: Modals ability, possibility, permission, advice ya necessity batate hain. Modal ke baad normally verb ka base form aata hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 can/could = ability/possibility \177 may/might = permission/possibility \177 should/ought to = advice \177 must/have to = necessity \177 would = conditional/polite usage Examples: 1. She can solve it. 2. You should revise . 3. You may leave . 4. Candidates must carry ID. 5. It might rain . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: He can goes n \256 He can go n . 16. Conditionals Simple Hinglish explanation: Conditional sentences 'if' situations batate hain. Pattern se pata chalta hai ki situation real/general hai, future possibility hai, imaginary hai ya past mein impossible ho chuki hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Zero: If + present, present. \177 First: If + present, will + base. \177 Second: If + past, would + base. \177 Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3. \177 Basic first conditional mein if ke turant baad normally will nahi aata. Examples: 1. If you heat ice, it melts . 2. If she studies, she will improve . 3. If I had time, I would practise . 4. If he had prepared, he would have succeeded .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 9 5. If I were you, I would revise . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: If she will study, she will pass n \256 If she studies, she will pass n . 17. Active and Passive Voice Simple Hinglish explanation: Active mein subject action karta hai. Passive mein action receive karne wali cheez focus ban jaati hai. Passive mein generally be + V3 structure use hota hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Present: is/am/are + V3 \177 Past: was/were + V3 \177 Future: will be + V3 \177 Modal: must/can/should be + V3 \177 Tense ko voice change karte waqt preserve karna hai. Examples: 1. They solve the problem \256 The problem is solved . 2. She wrote the letter \256 The letter was written . 3. They will announce the result \256 It will be announced . 4. You must complete it \256 It must be completed . 5. Someone stole the phone \256 The phone was stolen . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Voice change karte waqt tense change mat karo. 18. Direct and Indirect Speech Simple Hinglish explanation: Direct speech mein speaker ke exact words quotes mein hote hain. Indirect speech mein hum meaning report karte hain. Pronoun, tense, time words aur question structure change ho sakte hain. Yaad rakhna: \177 Statement: said that... \177 Yes/no question: asked if/whether... \177 Wh-question: asked + wh-word + statement order. \177 Command: told/ordered + object + to + verb. \177 Request: asked + object + to + verb. Examples: 1. \223I am ready.\224 \256 She said she was ready . 2. \223I finished.\224 \256 He said he had finished . 3. \223Are you ready?\224 \256 He asked whether I was ready . 4. \223Where do you live?\224 \256 She asked where I lived . 5. \223Open the door.\224 \256 He ordered me to open it. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Indirect question mein statement order: He asked where I lived n , not where did I live n . 19. Gerunds Simple Hinglish explanation: Gerund ek -ing form hota hai jo noun ki tarah behave karta hai. Kuch verbs ke baad gerund commonly use hota hai. Yaad rakhna:

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 10 \177 enjoy + ing \177 avoid + ing \177 finish + ing \177 preposition + ing \177 Gerund sentence ka subject bhi ho sakta hai. Examples: 1. Reading improves vocabulary. 2. She enjoys reading . 3. They avoided arguing . 4. He is interested in learning . 5. Practising daily improves speed. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: enjoy to read n \256 enjoy reading n . 20. Infinitives Simple Hinglish explanation: Full infinitive generally 'to + base verb' hota hai. Purpose, intention aur certain verb patterns mein use hota hai. Kuch structures mein bare infinitive aata hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Purpose: to improve. \177 want/decide/hope/plan + to + verb. \177 let/make + object + bare infinitive. \177 Modal + bare infinitive. \177 Noun ko describe karne ke liye infinitive aa sakta hai. Examples: 1. She studied to improve . 2. He decided to practise . 3. To learn takes patience. 4. Let him go . 5. I have a book to read . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: He made me to go n \256 He made me go n . 21. Participles Simple Hinglish explanation: Participles verb forms hain jo verb phrase ya adjective ki tarah use ho sakte hain. Present participle generally -ing hota hai; past participle usually V3 form hota hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 running water = present participle/adjectival use \177 broken glass = past participle/adjectival use \177 having finished = perfect participle \177 is studying = continuous verb \177 was written = passive verb Examples:

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 11 1. The shining stars looked beautiful. 2. The broken window was repaired. 3. Having finished the work, she left. 4. They are preparing . 5. The answer was written carefully. Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: Dangling modifier se bachna hai: Walking to college, the rain started n \227 rain walk nahi kar raha. 22. Question Tags Simple Hinglish explanation: Statement ke end mein chhota question add karna question tag hai. Positive statement ke saath usually negative tag aur negative statement ke saath positive tag aata hai. Yaad rakhna: \177 Same auxiliary/modal use karo. \177 Pronoun subject ke according match karo. \177 Simple present/past mein auxiliary na ho to do/does/did use karo. \177 Imperatives aur Let's ke special patterns hote hain. Examples: 1. She is ready, isn't she? 2. He isn't late, is he? 3. You can swim, can't you? 4. They finished, didn't they? 5. Open the window, will you? Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: She likes tea, isn't she? n \256 She likes tea, doesn't she? n 23. Parallelism Simple Hinglish explanation: Parallelism ka matlab hai list ya paired structure mein grammar ka same pattern maintain karna. Agar first item gerund hai, baaki bhi ideally gerund form mein hone chahiye. Yaad rakhna: \177 gerund + gerund + gerund \177 to + verb + to + verb + to + verb \177 noun + noun + noun \177 adjective + adjective + adjective \177 paired conjunctions mein balanced structure. Examples: 1. She likes reading, writing and travelling . 2. He wants to learn, to practise and to improve . 3. She is smart, disciplined and patient . 4. The job requires skill, patience and focus . 5. It is not only difficult but also time-consuming . Common mistake / exam tip: Trap: reading, writing and to travel n \256 reading, writing and travelling n .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 12 24. Commonly Confused Words Simple Hinglish explanation: Kuch English words similar dikhte ya sunai dete hain, lekin meaning different hota hai. Inhe isolated spelling ki jagah sentence context ke saath learn karo. Yaad rakhna: \177 its = possession; it's = it is/it has \177 their = possession; there = place; they're = they are \177 your = possession; you're = you are \177 affect = usually verb; effect = usually noun \177 principal = head/main; principle = rule/belief Examples: 1. It's raining; the company changed its policy. 2. They're waiting there with their books. 3. You're responsible for your work. 4. Sleep can affect focus; the effect was clear. 5. The principal explained the school's principle . Common mistake / exam tip: Trick: Contraction expand karo. 'it's' ko 'it is' se replace kar sakte ho? Agar haan, it's possible. Possession ho to its.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 13 25. ERROR SPOTTING \227 KAISE SOLVE KARNA HAI ELI5: Sentence ko parts mein tod diya gaya hai. Tumhe dekhna hai ki kis part mein grammar ka rule break hua hai. Pura sentence turant rewrite mat karo. Pehle error ka rule identify karo. Checking order: Subject + Verb \256 Pronoun \256 Article/Determiner \256 Tense \256 Preposition \256 Adjective/Adverb \256 Comparison \256 Parallelism \256 Meaning. Example 1: Each of the students / have submitted / their assignment / on time. Why? Part 2: have \256 has . 'Each' singular hai. Example 2: The list of topics / are / on the desk / near the window. Why? Part 2: are \256 is . Main subject 'list' hai. Example 3: She / is one of the best student / in the class / this year. Why? Part 2: student \256 students . One of the + plural noun. Example 4: The teacher asked / Rahul and I / to wait / outside. Why? Part 2: I \256 me . Yahan pronoun object hai. Example 5: She completed the assignment / quick / and submitted it / before lunch. Why? Part 2: quick \256 quickly . 'Completed' ko describe kar raha hai. Example 6: He is good / in mathematics / but weak / in English. Why? Part 2: in \256 at . Standard combination 'good at'. Example 7: He has completed / the work / yesterday / without help. Why? Part 3 ke saath tense mismatch. 'Yesterday' ke saath simple past: He completed the work yesterday. Example 8: The students / was waiting / outside the hall / for an hour. Why? Part 2: was \256 were . Students plural hai. CET source connection: Supplied MAH-MBA/MMS-CET material mein isi pattern mein sentence ko four parts mein break karke error/no-error identify karne ko diya gaya hai. n filecite n turn1file0 n L1-L8 n

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 14 26. CHOOSE THE CORRECT SENTENCE / SENTENCE IMPROVEMENT ELI5: Yahan options almost same dikhte hain. Tumhe meaning same rakhte hue grammatically correct aur natural option choose karna hai. Method: Pehle meaning samjho \256 subject/verb check \256 tense \256 pronoun \256 article \256 preposition \256 word order \256 unnecessary words. Example 1 A) She is a honest student. B) She is an honest student. C) She is honest a student. D) She is an honesty student. Explanation: B \227 honest vowel sound se start hota hai, isliye an. Example 2 A) Neither of the boys are ready. B) Neither of the boys is ready. C) Neither boys is ready. D) Neither of boys are ready. Explanation: B \227 neither singular verb leta hai. Example 3 A) He has went home. B) He has gone home. C) He had go home. D) He has going home. Explanation: B \227 has + V3; gone V3 hai. Example 4 A) I prefer tea than coffee. B) I prefer tea to coffee. C) I prefer tea from coffee. D) I prefer tea over than coffee. Explanation: B \227 prefer X to Y. Example 5 A) The news are surprising. B) The news is surprising. C) The news were surprising. D) The news have surprising. Explanation: B \227 news normally singular treat hota hai. Example 6 A) She is capable to solve it. B) She is capable of solving it. C) She is capable for solve it. D) She is capable solving it. Explanation: B \227 capable of + gerund. Example 7 A) One of my friend is preparing. B) One of my friends is preparing. C) One of my friends are preparing. D) One of my friend are preparing. Explanation: B \227 one of + plural noun + singular verb.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 Detailed Hinglish Grammar Guide Page 15 Example 8 A) She suggested me to study. B) She suggested that I study. C) She suggested me studying. D) She suggested to me study. Explanation: B \227 standard formal construction.

title: MHT CET MBA Full English Grammar Guide
contentSample: MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 FULL ENGLISH GRAMMAR GUIDE ELI5 explanations + formal English rules + 5 unique examples for every grammar topic + Error Spotting + Choose the Correct Sentence + 31 exam-relevant Figures of Speech Why this guide: The uploaded MAH-MBA/MMS-CET 2026 sample uses error identification and sentence correction/rewriting in Verb
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS \227 FULL ENGLISH GRAMMAR GUIDE ELI5 explanations + formal English rules + 5 unique examples for every grammar topic + Error Spotting + Choose the Correct Sentence + 31 exam-relevant Figures of Speech Why this guide: The uploaded MAH-MBA/MMS-CET 2026 sample uses error identification and sentence correction/rewriting in Verbal Ability, so those skills are explicitly covered here. The official sample also includes passage-based verbal questions. Important: \223All figures of speech\224 has no universally fixed finite list. This guide therefore covers a broad, exam-relevant set of 31 common figures and gives five examples for each.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 2 CONTENTS Grammar: Parts of Speech \177 Articles \177 Determiners \177 Nouns \177 Pronouns \177 Adjectives \177 Comparison \177 Adverbs \177 Verbs \177 Tenses \177 Subject\226Verb Agreement \177 Prepositions \177 Conjunctions \177 Phrases & Clauses \177 Modals \177 Conditionals \177 Active/Passive Voice \177 Direct/Indirect Speech \177 Gerunds \177 Infinitives \177 Participles \177 Question Tags \177 Parallelism \177 Confusing Words Exam skills: Error Spotting \177 Choose the Correct Sentence \177 Mixed revision strategy Figures of Speech: Simile \177 Metaphor \177 Personification \177 Hyperbole \177 Alliteration \177 Assonance \177 Consonance \177 Onomatopoeia \177 Oxymoron \177 Paradox \177 Irony \177 Sarcasm \177 Euphemism \177 Litotes \177 Antithesis \177 Anaphora \177 Epistrophe \177 Climax \177 Anticlimax \177 Pun \177 Allusion \177 Apostrophe \177 Metonymy \177 Synecdoche \177 Transferred Epithet \177 Rhetorical Question \177 Inversion \177 Pleonasm \177 Tautology \177 Pathetic Fallacy \177 Paronomasia

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 3 1. Parts of Speech ELI5: Words have jobs. A noun names, a pronoun replaces, a verb shows action/state, an adjective describes, an adverb modifies, a preposition shows relation, a conjunction joins and an interjection shows feeling. English/exam rule: Identify the grammatical job, not just the word itself. 5 unique examples: \177 The manager approved the plan. (noun) \177 She approved it. (pronoun) \177 The team celebrated . (verb) \177 It was a difficult test. (adjective) \177 She answered quickly . (adverb) 2. Articles ELI5: A/an means one but not a specific one; the points to a specific/known thing. English/exam rule: A/an depends on sound: a university , an hour , an MBA . 5 unique examples: \177 She bought a laptop. \177 He waited for an hour. \177 Close the window beside you. \177 She is a university student. \177 Books can change lives. (general) 3. Determiners ELI5: Determiners tell us which one, how many, how much or whose. English/exam rule: Common: this/that, these/those, some/any, much/many, few/little, each/every, either/neither, my/your. 5 unique examples: \177 This question is easier. \177 There are many candidates. \177 We do not have much time. \177 Only a few students left. \177 Each participant received a badge. 4. Nouns ELI5: Nouns name people, places, things, ideas, qualities or groups. English/exam rule: Check singular/plural, countable/uncountable, collective and possessive forms. 5 unique examples: \177 The teacher explained the rule. \177 Mumbai is a busy city . \177 The calculator is here. \177 Honesty builds trust. \177 The team celebrated its win. 5. Pronouns ELI5: Pronouns avoid repeating nouns.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 4 English/exam rule: Check subject/object, possessive, reflexive and relative pronouns. 5 unique examples: \177 She completed the assignment. \177 The coach praised him . \177 This seat is mine . \177 He prepared it himself . \177 The student who won smiled. 6. Adjectives ELI5: Adjectives describe nouns/pronouns. Ask: what kind, which one, how many? English/exam rule: Watch adjective order and comparison; avoid double comparatives. 5 unique examples: \177 A clear explanation. \177 A large hall. \177 Five questions. \177 An interesting lecture. \177 The broken chair. 7. Comparison of Adjectives ELI5: Positive describes; comparative compares two; superlative compares three or more. English/exam rule: Use taller/tallest or more useful/most useful. Avoid more better/most best. 5 unique examples: \177 This book is useful . \177 This is more useful than that one. \177 This is the most useful book. \177 Today is better than yesterday. \177 That was the worst mistake. 8. Adverbs ELI5: Adverbs commonly tell how, when, where or how often. English/exam rule: Many end in -ly, but fast, hard, late and well can also be adverbs. 5 unique examples: \177 She spoke clearly . \177 We leave tomorrow . \177 Wait outside . \177 He often practises. \177 It was very difficult. 9. Verbs ELI5: Verbs show action, state or occurrence. English/exam rule: Check main/helping/modal verbs, tense and form. 5 unique examples: \177 They solved the puzzle.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 5 \177 She knows the answer. \177 He is studying. \177 You should revise. \177 She opened the door. 10. Tenses ELI5: Tense tells when an action/state happens. English/exam rule: Learn simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous; use time markers as clues. 5 unique examples: \177 She studies every evening. \177 She is studying now. \177 She studied yesterday. \177 She had finished before dinner. \177 She will study tomorrow. 11. Subject\226Verb Agreement ELI5: The verb must match the real subject in number. English/exam rule: Each/every/neither/either normally take singular verbs; ignore distracting phrases between subject and verb. 5 unique examples: \177 The student is ready. \177 The students are ready. \177 Each player has a jersey. \177 Neither answer is correct. \177 The box of books is heavy. 12. Prepositions ELI5: Prepositions show place, time, direction or relationship. English/exam rule: Memorise fixed combinations such as good at, interested in, responsible for, depend on, capable of. 5 unique examples: \177 Keys are on the table. \177 Class starts at 9. \177 She walked towards the gate. \177 He is interested in finance. \177 Success depends on practice. 13. Conjunctions ELI5: Conjunctions join words, phrases or clauses. English/exam rule: Know coordinating, subordinating and correlative conjunctions. 5 unique examples: \177 Riya and Aman prepared. \177 He was tired, but continued. \177 She stayed home because it rained. \177 Either study now or revise later.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 6 \177 Although it was late, they continued. 14. Phrases & Clauses ELI5: A phrase is not a complete clause; a clause has a subject and verb. English/exam rule: Recognise independent, dependent, relative and adverb clauses. 5 unique examples: \177 The girl in the blue dress smiled. \177 She smiled. \177 Because she was happy , she smiled. \177 The book that you gave me is useful. \177 We left when the rain stopped . 15. Modals ELI5: Modals show ability, possibility, permission, advice or necessity. English/exam rule: Modal + base verb: can go, should study, must finish. 5 unique examples: \177 She can solve it. \177 You should revise. \177 You may leave. \177 Candidates must carry ID. \177 It might rain. 16. Conditionals ELI5: Conditionals link a condition with a result. English/exam rule: Zero: present/present; first: present/will; second: past/would; third: had + V3/would have + V3. 5 unique examples: \177 If you heat ice, it melts . \177 If she studies, she will improve . \177 If I had time, I would practise . \177 If he had prepared, he would have succeeded . \177 If she had slept earlier, she would feel better now. 17. Active & Passive Voice ELI5: Active focuses on the doer; passive focuses on the receiver. English/exam rule: Passive normally uses be + past participle and preserves the tense. 5 unique examples: \177 They solve the problem \256 It is solved . \177 She wrote the letter \256 It was written . \177 They will announce the result \256 It will be announced . \177 You must complete it \256 It must be completed . \177 Who wrote the report? \256 By whom was it written? 18. Direct & Indirect Speech ELI5: Direct speech quotes exact words; indirect speech reports them.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 7 English/exam rule: Watch pronouns, tense backshift, time words and question structure. 5 unique examples: \177 \223I am ready.\224 \256 She said she was ready . \177 \223I finished.\224 \256 He said he had finished . \177 \223Are you ready?\224 \256 He asked whether I was ready . \177 \223Where do you live?\224 \256 She asked where I lived . \177 \223Open the door.\224 \256 He ordered me to open it. 19. Gerunds ELI5: A gerund is an -ing form functioning as a noun. English/exam rule: Common after enjoy, avoid, finish, suggest, mind and practise. 5 unique examples: \177 Reading improves vocabulary. \177 She enjoys reading . \177 He is interested in learning . \177 They avoided arguing . \177 I appreciate your helping me. 20. Infinitives ELI5: An infinitive is usually to + base verb; it can express purpose or follow certain verbs. English/exam rule: Know want to, decide to, hope to, plan to and bare infinitive after let/make. 5 unique examples: \177 She studied to improve . \177 He decided to practise . \177 To learn takes patience. \177 I have a book to read . \177 Let him go . 21. Participles ELI5: Participles are verb forms used in verb phrases or as adjectives. English/exam rule: Watch -ing vs past participle and avoid dangling modifiers. 5 unique examples: \177 The shining stars looked beautiful. \177 The broken window was repaired. \177 Having finished , she left. \177 They are preparing . \177 The answer was written carefully. 22. Question Tags ELI5: A short question is added to a statement; positive normally takes negative and vice versa. English/exam rule: Use the same auxiliary/modal and matching pronoun. 5 unique examples: \177 She is ready, isn\222t she?

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 8 \177 He isn\222t late, is he? \177 You can swim, can\222t you? \177 They finished, didn\222t they? \177 Open the window, will you? 23. Parallelism ELI5: Items joined together should have the same grammatical shape. English/exam rule: Keep forms parallel after and, or, either-or, not only-but also. 5 unique examples: \177 She likes reading, writing and travelling . \177 He wants to learn, to practise and to improve . \177 Wrong: reading, writing and to travel ; right: travelling . \177 The course is interesting as well as practical . \177 It is not only difficult but also time-consuming . 24. Common Confusing Words ELI5: Similar-looking/sounding words can have different meanings. English/exam rule: Learn them as pairs and use context. 5 unique examples: \177 It\222s raining; the company changed its policy. \177 They\222re waiting there with their books. \177 You\222re responsible for your work. \177 Sleep can affect focus; the effect was obvious. \177 The principal explained the school\222s principle .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 9 25. ERROR SPOTTING \227 HOW TO SOLVE ELI5: A sentence is split into parts. One part may contain a grammar mistake. Find it; if all parts are correct, choose No Error. Order of checking: Subject \256 Verb \256 Pronoun \256 Article/Determiner \256 Preposition \256 Adjective/Adverb \256 Tense \256 Parallelism. 1. Each of the players / have received / a certificate / after the event. Answer: Part 2: have \256 has . Each is singular. 2. She / is one of the best student / in the class / this year. Answer: Part 2: student \256 students . One of the + plural noun. 3. Neither of the answers / are / correct / according to the key. Answer: Part 2: are \256 is in standard exam grammar. 4. He is good / in mathematics / but weak / in English. Answer: Part 2: in \256 at ; we say good at. 5. She completed the work / quick / and submitted it / before lunch. Answer: Part 2: quick \256 quickly ; the word modifies the verb. 6. The teacher asked / Rahul and I / to wait / outside. Answer: Part 2: I \256 me ; object of asked. 7. He has completed / the assignment / yesterday / without help. Answer: Part 3 creates a tense mismatch; use simple past: He completed the assignment yesterday. 8. The list of topics / are / on the desk / near the window. Answer: Part 2: are \256 is ; subject is list. The uploaded MAH-MBA/MMS-CET 2026 sample explicitly uses the broken-into-parts error-identification format and includes No Error as an option.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 10 26. CHOOSE THE CORRECT SENTENCE ELI5: The options are almost identical. Compare them word-by-word. Check agreement, tense, article, pronoun, preposition and word order. 1. A) She is a honest student. B) She is an honest student. C) She is honest a student. D) She is an honesty student. Answer: B \227 honest begins with a vowel sound. 2. A) Neither of the boys are ready. B) Neither of the boys is ready. C) Neither boys is ready. D) Neither of boys are ready. Answer: B \227 neither is singular here. 3. A) He has went home. B) He has gone home. C) He had go home. D) He has going home. Answer: B \227 has + past participle. 4. A) I prefer tea than coffee. B) I prefer tea to coffee. C) I prefer tea from coffee. D) I prefer tea over than coffee. Answer: B \227 standard pattern: prefer X to Y. 5. A) The news are surprising. B) The news is surprising. C) The news were surprising. D) The news have surprising. Answer: B \227 news is treated as singular. 6. A) She is capable to solve it. B) She is capable of solving it. C) She is capable for solve it. D) She is capable solving it. Answer: B \227 capable of + gerund. 7. A) One of my friend is preparing. B) One of my friends is preparing. C) One of my friends are preparing. D) One of my friend are preparing. Answer: B \227 one of + plural noun + singular verb. 8. A) She suggested me to study. B) She suggested that I study. C) She suggested me studying. D) She suggested to me study. Answer: B \227 standard formal construction.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 11 27. FIGURES OF SPEECH \227 EXAM-RELEVANT SET There is no single universally agreed finite list of every figure of speech. The set below covers the major/common forms useful for entrance-exam identification. Each has five examples. Simile Meaning: Comparison using like/as 1. Her smile was like sunshine . 2. He slept like a log . 3. She ran as fast as the wind . 4. The room was like an oven . 5. Her voice was as soft as silk . Metaphor Meaning: Direct comparison without like/as 1. Time is a thief . 2. Her voice was music . 3. The city is a jungle . 4. His words were arrows . 5. Knowledge is power . Personification Meaning: Giving human qualities to non-human things 1. The wind whispered . 2. The alarm clock screamed . 3. The moon watched us. 4. Opportunity knocked . 5. The old house groaned . Hyperbole Meaning: Deliberate exaggeration 1. I told you a million times . 2. This bag weighs a ton . 3. She waited forever . 4. He was dying of embarrassment . 5. That was the hardest exam on Earth . Alliteration Meaning: Repeated initial consonant sound 1. Wild winds whistle . 2. Peter picked purple plums . 3. Busy bees buzzed . 4. Silver snakes slid . 5. Bright blue balloons floated. Assonance Meaning: Repeated vowel sound 1. The light of the fire shone bright.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 12 2. The mellow wedding bells rang. 3. The cool moon moved slowly. 4. He tried to hide the sign. 5. The rainy day faded away. Consonance Meaning: Repeated consonant sound within/end of words 1. The stroke of luck helped. 2. The blank and think pattern repeats a consonant sound. 3. The lumpy, bumpy road shook. 4. The wind bent the tent . 5. The crisp clasp snapped. Onomatopoeia Meaning: A word imitates a sound 1. The door went bang . 2. The bees buzzed . 3. The clock went tick-tock . 4. Water sizzled . 5. The snake hissed . Oxymoron Meaning: Contradictory words together 1. deafening silence 2. bittersweet memory 3. jumbo shrimp 4. living dead 5. seriously funny Paradox Meaning: Apparently contradictory statement with a deeper idea 1. Less is more. 2. The more you learn, the less you know. 3. The only constant is change. 4. To save money, you sometimes spend money. 5. Freedom requires rules. Irony Meaning: Contrast between expectation/reality or literal/intended meaning 1. A fire station burns down. 2. A traffic officer gets a speeding ticket. 3. A dentist has terrible teeth. 4. A weather expert forgets an umbrella in rain. 5. After disaster: What a perfect result. Sarcasm Meaning: Mocking or cutting irony

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 13 1. After a huge mistake: Brilliant job! 2. To someone late: Nice of you to join us. 3. During rain: Perfect beach weather. 4. After breaking a printer: Exactly what we needed. 5. Seeing a messy desk: Beautiful organisation. Euphemism Meaning: Softer expression for an unpleasant idea 1. passed away = died 2. let go = fired 3. between jobs = unemployed 4. economical with the truth = lying 5. senior citizen = elderly person Litotes Meaning: Understatement through negation 1. It is not bad . 2. She is not unfamiliar with it. 3. That was no small achievement . 4. He is not unintelligent . 5. The result is not insignificant . Antithesis Meaning: Balanced contrast of opposing ideas 1. Speech is silver; silence is golden. 2. Many are called, few are chosen. 3. Easy to begin, hard to finish. 4. Hope for the best, prepare for the worst. 5. Small step, giant leap. Anaphora Meaning: Repetition at the beginning 1. We will learn. We will practise. 2. Every day she reads; every day she writes. 3. This is our time; this is our chance. 4. I want focus; I want discipline. 5. Never give up; never stop learning. Epistrophe Meaning: Repetition at the end 1. We work for success , study for success . 2. They asked for justice , fought for justice . 3. She wanted to learn , lived to learn . 4. We prepare for today , work for today . 5. He spoke with courage , acted with courage . Climax

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 14 Meaning: Ideas rise in intensity 1. He whispered, spoke, shouted. 2. She learned, practised, mastered. 3. He risked time, money, reputation. 4. The problem became difficult, serious, disastrous. 5. A spark became a flame, then a wildfire. Anticlimax Meaning: Build-up suddenly drops to something trivial 1. He trained for months and forgot his shoes. 2. She expected a grand surprise and received a pen. 3. The speech promised revolution and ended with a coupon. 4. He solved the crisis and lost his lunch. 5. They planned an epic trip and stayed in the lobby. Pun Meaning: Wordplay using double meaning/similar sounds 1. A bicycle cannot stand because it is two-tired . 2. The calendar\222s days are numbered . 3. A boiled egg is hard to beat . 4. The banker lost interest . 5. The math teacher has too many problems . Allusion Meaning: Indirect reference to a known person/place/story/event 1. He met his Waterloo . 2. She is a Romeo . 3. It became our Trojan horse . 4. He has the patience of Job . 5. She opened a Pandora\222s box . Apostrophe Meaning: Direct address to an absent person/object/idea 1. O Time , slow down! 2. Dear Moon , light my path. 3. O Justice , where are you? 4. Death , do not take him yet. 5. Freedom , we value you. Metonymy Meaning: A related thing stands for the thing meant 1. The crown announced a decision. 2. The White House issued a statement. 3. The press asked questions. 4. The bench delivered its ruling. 5. The stage applauded her work.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar & Figures of Speech Page 15 Synecdoche Meaning: Part represents whole or whole represents part 1. All hands on deck. 2. More boots on the ground. 3. Nice wheels . 4. Many new faces arrived. 5. We need more hands for the project. Transferred Epithet Meaning: Adjective is attached to one noun but logically describes another 1. A sleepless night . 2. The angry streets were crowded. 3. A restless journey . 4. A miserable holiday . 5. A thoughtful look . Rhetorical Question Meaning: Question asked for effect, not a real answer 1. Who doesn\222t want success? 2. How could I forget you? 3. Isn\222t this amazing? 4. What is more important than time? 5. Do we really need another excuse? Inversion Meaning: Unusual/reversed word order for emphasis 1. Never have I seen such a view. 2. Rarely does she complain. 3. Down came the rain. 4. Only then did he understand. 5. So difficult was the test that many struggled. Pleonasm Meaning: More words than necessary; meaning repeats 1. free gift 2. final conclusion 3. past history 4. advance planning 5. new innovation Tautology Meaning: Same idea repeated in different words 1. each and every 2. null and void 3. first and foremost 4. safe and sound

title: MHT CET MBA Reading Comprehension DETAILED MASTER GUIDE HINGLISH
contentSample: MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS READING COMPREHENSION \001 DETAILED MASTER GUIDE Expanded Hinglish Theory \002 Question Types \002 Deep Strategies \002 Elimination \002 Speed \002 Error Analysis Purpose of this guide Yeh guide Reading Comprehension ko zero se exam-ready level tak samjhane ke liye hai. Isme sirf 'passage kaise padhein' nahi, b
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS READING COMPREHENSION \001 DETAILED MASTER GUIDE Expanded Hinglish Theory \002 Question Types \002 Deep Strategies \002 Elimination \002 Speed \002 Error Analysis Purpose of this guide Yeh guide Reading Comprehension ko zero se exam-ready level tak samjhane ke liye hai. Isme sirf 'passage kaise padhein' nahi, balki har major question type ko identify karna, evidence locate karna, wrong options eliminate karna, inference aur tone ko accurately judge karna, aur timed practice mein mistakes ko analyse karna explain kiya gaya hai. 1. Reading Comprehension ka basic concept Reading Comprehension (RC) ka simple meaning hai: jo padha hai usko accurately samajhna aur us understanding ke basis par correct conclusion tak pahunchna. Exam mein RC sirf English reading ka test nahi hota. Isme simultaneously reading speed, vocabulary, logical reasoning, attention to detail, author ke viewpoint ko samajhna aur options ko compare karne ki ability test hoti hai. RC mein exactly kya test hota hai? \002 Understanding: Passage actually kya keh raha hai? \002 Structure: Ideas kis order mein develop hue? \002 Evidence: Kaunsi line/idea kisi answer ko support karti hai? \002 Inference: Passage se logically kya conclude kiya ja sakta hai? \002 Evaluation: Kaunsa option passage ke according strongest fit hai? \002 Language: Word ya phrase ka meaning context mein kya hai? Most important mindset RC mein tumhe author se agree/disagree nahi karna. Tumhe author ko accurately understand karna hai. Personal opinion ko side par rakho. 2. Passage ka anatomy \001 passage ke andar kya hota hai? Ek well-written passage usually ek central topic ke around multiple ideas develop karta hai. Har paragraph ka ek role ho sakta hai. Passage Part Possible Role Tumhe kya identify karna hai? Opening Topic / background / problem Passage kis issue se start ho raha hai? Development Explanation / causes / evidence Author idea ko kaise develop kar raha hai? Comparison Two views / methods / situations Similarity/difference kya hai? Counterpoint Opposite view / limitation Author kis objection ko address kar raha hai? Conclusion Implication / summary / suggestion Final takeaway kya hai? Paragraph ko ek sentence mein compress karo Har paragraph padhne ke baad mentally ek mini-label banao. Example: P1 = Problem, P2 = Cause, P3 = Evidence, P4 = Counterargument, P5 = Conclusion. Isse long passage ko dobara poora reread karne ki need kam hoti hai. 3. Reading ka 3-pass method

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 2 Pass 1 \001 Orientation First reading ka purpose har word yaad karna nahi hai. Bas topic, author ka direction aur paragraph structure samjho. \002 Title ho to read karo. \002 First paragraph ka central idea pakdo. \002 Har next paragraph ka role identify karo. \002 Contrast words aur conclusion signals notice karo. Pass 2 \001 Question-driven reading Questions dekho aur identify karo ki kis paragraph/idea ki zarurat hai. Detail questions ke liye targeted rereading karo. Pass 3 \001 Verification Final option select karne se pehle passage evidence se verify karo. Especially inference, tone, purpose aur close options mein yeh step important hai. Important Har passage ko teen baar mechanically read karna zaroori nahi. Easy passage mein one careful reading + targeted lookup enough ho sakta hai. Difficult passage mein targeted rereading use karo. 4. Main Idea / Central Idea \001 deepest explanation Main idea poore passage ka central message hota hai. Yeh 'passage kis topic par hai?' se ek level deeper hota hai. Topic vs Main Idea Term Example Topic Online education Main Idea Online education can expand access to learning, but its effectiveness depends on design, engagement and support. Topic ek subject hai. Main idea batata hai ki author us subject ke baare mein kya keh raha hai. Main idea identify karne ka 5-step method \002 Har paragraph ka one-line summary banao. \002 Common idea identify karo jo multiple paragraphs mein repeat/develop ho raha hai. \002 Author kis point ko explain/support/criticize kar raha hai dekho. \002 Examples ko remove karke underlying claim identify karo. \002 Options mein woh statement choose karo jo whole passage ko accurately cover kare. Main idea ke classic traps \002 Detail trap: ek example ko whole passage bana diya. \002 Topic trap: sirf subject diya, author's message nahi. \002 Extreme trap: passage se zyada strong claim. \002 Outside-scope trap: related but passage mein discussed nahi. \002 Partial trap: first/last paragraph cover karta hai but whole development miss karta hai. 5. Specific Fact / Detail Questions Yeh questions passage ke directly stated information par based hote hain. Inmein imagination ki zarurat nahi; location aur verification ki zarurat hai. Method \002 Question ke 1\0033 unique keywords identify karo. \002 Passage mein exact word ya synonym locate karo. \002 Us sentence ke pehle aur baad ka context padho.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 3 \002 Option ko original statement ke against compare karo. \002 Agar option mein ek extra unsupported clause hai, carefully reject karo. Detail-question trap Option ka first half passage mein correct ho sakta hai, lekin second half unsupported ho. Whole option verify karo, sirf first phrase nahi. 6. Inference \001 RC ka most misunderstood area Inference ka matlab hai: passage mein statement directly nahi diya gaya, lekin available evidence se ek reasonable conclusion nikalta hai. Direct statement vs inference Type Example Direct The passage says that remote work reduced commuting time. Inference Remote work can potentially improve employees' daily time availability. Unsupported Remote work always makes employees more productive. Inference ko support karne ke liye passage mein sufficient evidence hona chahiye. 'Could', 'may', 'suggests' jaise cautious conclusions often inference questions mein relevant ho sakte hain, lekin option passage se justified hona chahiye. Inference test Ask yourself \004Agar passage ki saari information true maan loon, kya yeh option logically follow hota hai?\005 Agar answer clearly yes nahi hai, option risky hai. Inference traps \002 Outside knowledge \002 Extreme certainty \002 Author ki unstated intention assume karna \002 Ek isolated example ko universal rule banana \002 Emotion-based conclusion \002 Cause assume karna jab passage sirf correlation batata ho 7. Author's Purpose \001 WHY? Purpose ka question poochta hai: Author ne yeh passage kis objective se likha? Purpose Typical signals Inform Facts, background, data, neutral explanation Explain How/why something works or happens Compare Two or more ideas/methods side-by-side Criticize Weakness, limitation, failure highlight Persuade Reader ko particular view accept karne ki direction Evaluate Strengths and weaknesses assess Suggest Solution, recommendation, possible action Warn Risk/consequence highlight Purpose aur main idea same nahi hain. Main idea = what the passage says. Purpose = why the author says it.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 4 8. Author's Tone \001 attitude identify karna Tone author ki attitude ya emotional/intellectual stance hai. Tone identify karte waqt individual words se zyada overall language pattern dekho. Tone Meaning Common clues Neutral / Objective Balanced, factual measured language, facts Critical Weakness point out problem, failure, limitation Skeptical Doubtful questions, reservations Optimistic Positive expectation potential, opportunity, promising Pessimistic Negative expectation risk, decline, failure Cautious Careful, qualified may, might, however, limited Appreciative Praise valuable, effective, significant Concerned Worry about issue risk, threat, concern Sarcastic Mocking/ironic opposite surface meaning/context Urgent Immediate importance must, immediate, pressing Tone kaise decide karein? \002 Author ke adjectives/adverbs dekho. \002 Positive/negative words ka overall balance dekho. \002 Author claims ko confidently ya cautiously present karta hai? \002 Kya author criticism kar raha hai ya merely describing? \002 Ek single strong word se tone decide mat karo. 9. Vocabulary in Context RC mein difficult vocabulary ka question aa sakta hai, lekin yahan dictionary memorisation se zyada context important hai. Context clues ke 6 types \002 Definition clue: passage word ka meaning directly explain karta hai. \002 Example clue: examples meaning reveal karte hain. \002 Contrast clue: however, unlike, whereas etc. \002 Cause/effect clue: result se meaning infer hota hai. \002 Synonym clue: nearby similar word. \002 Overall tone clue: paragraph positive hai ya negative? 4-step contextual meaning method \002 Word ko mentally replace karo. \002 Sentence ka grammar preserve hona chahiye. \002 Positive/negative sense match karo. \002 Nearby context ke saath option test karo. Important Word ka dictionary meaning aur passage ka contextual meaning slightly different ho sakta hai. Question context mein most appropriate meaning pooch raha hota hai. 10. Reference / Pronoun Questions Words such as it, they, this, these, such, former, latter, that kisi earlier idea/person/object ko refer kar sakte hain.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS \001 Reading Comprehension Detailed Master Guide Page 5 Solve kaise karein? \002 Nearest noun se start karo, but blindly choose mat karo. \002 Singular/plural match check karo. \002 Meaning logically fit hai ya nahi check karo. \002 Entire sentence read karke reference confirm karo. Rule: Grammatical match + logical match dono required hain. 11. Best Title Questions Best title passage ke overall topic aur central message ko concise form mein capture karta hai. Title select karne ka formula Best Title = Topic + Central Focus + Correct Scope \002 Too narrow title reject. \002 Too broad title reject. \002 Interesting but unsupported title reject. \002 Aisa title choose karo jo passage ke maximum content ko naturally cover kare. 12. Negative Questions \001 NOT / EXCEPT / INCORRECT Red-alert words Question mein NOT, EXCEPT, INCORRECT, FALSE, LEAST, CANNOT aaye to mentally us word ko highlight karo. Bohot baar student passage samajhne ke baad bhi question direction miss karke wrong option select karta hai. Aise questions mein pehle question ko positive form mein mentally convert karna useful hai. Example: 'All are mentioned EXCEPT' \006 teen supported options identify karo; remaining option answer hoga. 13. Compare & Contrast Questions Passage do theories, technologies, generations, systems, policies, approaches ya viewpoints compare kar sakta hai. Comparison map Question Check What is common? Shared feature How are they different? Specific distinction Which is more effective? Only if passage explicitly/evidentially supports comparison Why does author mention B? Role of B in argument What changes between A and B? Direction of difference 14. Cause\002Effect Questions Cause = reason/trigger. Effect = outcome/result. Passage mein cause-effect relationship explicitly stated ya logically supported ho sakta hai. Do not confuse Sequence \007 Cause. Agar A pehle hua aur B baad mein hua, iska matlab automatically A caused B nahi hai. \002 Look for because, due to, leads to, results in, therefore, consequently. \002 Check whether author says causation or merely association. \002 Cause-effect direction reverse mat karo. 15. Statement / Conclusion Questions Kabhi question poochta hai ki passage se kaunsa conclusion best supported hai.
