Each topic is explained through definitions, recognition me
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS VOCABULARY MASTER GUIDE List of Words | Words Confused & Misused | Phobias | Manias | Prefixes & Suffixes | Analogies | Synonyms | Antonyms | One Word Substitution | Idioms & Phrases This guide is arranged according to the vocabulary syllabus headings supplied for preparation. Each topic is explained through definitions, recognition methods, examples, common distinctions, and examination-oriented approaches. Preparation approach What to learn Meaning first Understand what the word or expression actually means. Usage second See how it behaves in a sentence and what words commonly accompany it. Recognition third Learn roots, patterns, relationships, and common traps. Practice last Apply the knowledge in MCQs, context questions, analogies, and sentence-based questions. Vocabulary is most useful when a word is learned together with meaning, context, related words, and a realistic example.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 2 CONTENTS Section Topic Core subtopics 2.1 List of Words Meaning, context, word families, parts of speech, roots, usage, word relationships 2.2 Words Confused & Misused Commonly confused pairs, pronunciation traps, meaning traps, grammar/usage traps 2.3 Phobias Definition, root patterns, common phobias, identification questions 2.4 Manias Definition, root patterns, common manias, identification questions 2.5 Prefixes & Suffixes Meaning, types, common prefixes, common suffixes, word-building method 2.6 Analogies Meaning, relationship types, solving method, common traps 2.7 Synonyms Definition, shades of meaning, context, synonym families, traps 2.8 Antonyms Definition, types of opposites, context, common pairs, traps 2.9 One Word Substitution People, places, beliefs, professions, habits, time, events, descriptions 2.10 Idioms / Phrases Literal vs actual meaning, categories, usage, common expressions, traps Revision framework \001 Learn the definition in one clear sentence. \001 Connect it to a familiar Hindi/Hinglish idea where useful, but answer using the exact English meaning. \001 Read at least one example sentence. \001 Compare close alternatives before moving to the next word. \001 Test recall after a gap instead of rereading continuously.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 3 SECTION 2.1 - LIST OF WORDS (22-26) What this section covers: This section builds the core vocabulary bank. The objective is not only to know a dictionary definition but to recognise how a word behaves in context. A strong vocabulary entry has seven parts: the word, part of speech, core meaning, Hinglish meaning, example, synonym/antonym, and a common usage note. How to study a word \001 Step 1: Read the word and say it aloud. \001 Step 2: Reduce the definition to one simple idea. \001 Step 3: attach a familiar Hinglish interpretation. \001 Step 4: read the example sentence and identify the context. \001 Step 5: connect the word with a synonym or antonym. \001 Step 6: note any confusing word with which it is commonly mixed. Word families A word often appears in several forms. Recognising the family reduces memorisation and improves sentence completion. Base word Noun Adjective Verb Adverb success success successful succeed successfully decision decision decisive decide decisively beauty beauty beautiful beautify beautifully danger danger dangerous endanger dangerously High-value core words Word Abundant Meaning Present in large quantity Hinglish meaning bahut zyada matra mein Example The district has abundant rainfall. Synonym plentiful Antonym scarce Common trap Do not confuse abundant with sufficient; abundant means a large amount.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 4 Word Adverse Meaning Unfavourable or harmful Hinglish meaning pratikool / nuksan pahunchane wala Example The project faced adverse weather conditions. Synonym unfavourable Antonym favourable Common trap Adverse is usually used for things or conditions; a person is generally averse, not adverse. Word Alleviate Meaning Make something less severe Hinglish meaning tez dard ya problem ko kam karna Example The new policy may alleviate the pressure on students. Synonym relieve Antonym aggravate Common trap Alleviate reduces severity; it does not mean completely remove. Word Ambiguous Meaning Open to more than one interpretation Hinglish meaning jiska meaning clear na ho Example The statement was ambiguous. Synonym unclear Antonym unambiguous Common trap Ambiguous does not mean difficult; it means capable of multiple interpretations. Word Benevolent Meaning Kind and helpful Hinglish meaning dayalu aur bhalaai karne wala Example The benevolent donor supported the school. Synonym kind Antonym malevolent Common trap Benevolent is associated with goodwill and kindness.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 5 Word Candid Meaning Honest and straightforward Hinglish meaning seedha aur imaandaar Example She gave a candid opinion about the proposal. Synonym frank Antonym evasive Common trap Candid does not mean rude; the focus is openness and honesty. Word Coherent Meaning Logical and well connected Hinglish meaning baaton ka logically connected hona Example His explanation was coherent and easy to follow. Synonym logical Antonym incoherent Common trap Coherent refers to clear connection among ideas. Word Conspicuous Meaning Very noticeable Hinglish meaning jo easily notice ho jaye Example The bright sign was conspicuous from a distance. Synonym noticeable Antonym inconspicuous Common trap Conspicuous means easy to notice, not necessarily attractive. Word Diligent Meaning Showing steady and careful effort Hinglish meaning mehnati aur consistently careful Example The diligent student revised every chapter. Synonym industrious Antonym negligent Common trap Diligence is about sustained effort, not simply intelligence.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 6 Word Eloquent Meaning Fluent and persuasive in expression Hinglish meaning achhi aur prabhavshali expression wali language Example The speaker gave an eloquent address. Synonym articulate Antonym inarticulate Common trap Eloquent normally refers to effective expression, especially speaking or writing. Word Frugal Meaning Careful with money or resources Hinglish meaning paise/resources ko soch samajhkar use karna Example She is frugal and avoids unnecessary spending. Synonym thrifty Antonym wasteful Common trap Frugal is not the same as miserly; it can be a positive quality. Word Imminent Meaning Likely to happen very soon Hinglish meaning bahut jaldi hone wala Example A severe storm is imminent. Synonym impending Antonym remote Common trap Imminent concerns an event expected soon. Word Meticulous Meaning Very careful about details Hinglish meaning har detail ko bahut dhyan se dekhna Example He is meticulous about checking documents. Synonym careful Antonym careless Common trap Meticulous emphasises attention to small details.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 7 Word Obsolete Meaning No longer in use Hinglish meaning purana aur ab use mein nahi Example The machine became obsolete after the new technology arrived. Synonym outdated Antonym current Common trap Obsolete means replaced or no longer useful in its context. Word Pragmatic Meaning Practical and focused on workable results Hinglish meaning practical aur result-focused Example She took a pragmatic approach to the problem. Synonym practical Antonym impractical Common trap Pragmatic is about what works in practice. Word Reluctant Meaning Unwilling or hesitant Hinglish meaning mann na hona / hesitant hona Example He was reluctant to accept the offer. Synonym unwilling Antonym eager Common trap Reluctant does not mean unable; the person simply does not want to or is hesitant. Word Scrutinise Meaning Examine very carefully Hinglish meaning bahut dhyan se jaanchna Example The auditor scrutinised the records. Synonym examine Antonym overlook Common trap Scrutinise is stronger than simply look at.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 8 Word Vigilant Meaning Watchful and alert Hinglish meaning satark aur alert Example Security staff remained vigilant throughout the event. Synonym alert Antonym careless Common trap Vigilant describes continued alertness. Word Viable Meaning Capable of working successfully Hinglish meaning jo practically kaam kar sakta ho Example The team proposed a viable business model. Synonym feasible Antonym unworkable Common trap Viable is frequently used for plans, options, or systems that can work. Word Wary Meaning Cautious because of possible danger Hinglish meaning savdhan rehna Example Be wary of suspicious messages. Synonym cautious Antonym trusting Common trap Wary means cautious; weary means tired. Context-based understanding A word can have a slightly different force depending on the sentence. For vocabulary questions, read the entire sentence before selecting an option. A familiar word is not automatically the correct word if its context does not fit. Example: "The report was candid " suggests frankness. "The report was ambiguous " suggests that its meaning was unclear. Both may sound like descriptions of a report, but they describe different qualities.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 9 SECTION 2.2 - WORDS CONFUSED & MISUSED (27-31) These words are often confused because they look similar, sound similar, or are commonly used incorrectly. The safest method is to learn the difference in meaning and the grammatical role at the same time. A useful rule is to compare the words in pairs and immediately create one sentence for each.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 10 High-frequency confusion pairs Words Difference Example Memory cue Affect / Effect Affect is usually a verb meaning influence. Effect is usually a noun meaning result. Lack of sleep affects concentration. The effect was visible. Affect -> action; Effect -> result. Accept / Except Accept means receive or agree. Except means excluding. She accepted the offer. Everyone came except Arjun. Ask: receive/agree or leave out? Advice / Advise Advice is a noun. Advise is a verb. He gave useful advice . I advise you to revise. Advice = thing; Advise = action. Principal / Principle Principal can mean head of a school or most important. Principle means a rule or belief. The principal spoke about discipline. Honesty is a principle . Principal -> person/main; Principle -> rule. Compliment / Complement Compliment is praise. Complement means complete or improve by fitting well. She complimented my presentation. The colour complements the design. Compliment = praise; Complement = complete/fit. Stationary / Stationery Stationary means not moving. Stationery means writing materials. The car remained stationary . I bought office stationery . -ary -> not moving; -ery -> writing materials. Loose / Lose Loose means not tight. Lose means fail to keep, misplace, or not win. The belt is loose . Do not lose your confidence. Loose has two o letters; lose has one o after l. Then / Than Then usually refers to time or sequence. Than is used in comparisons. Study first, then revise. She is taller than me. Time/sequence -> then; comparison -> than. Their / There / They're Their shows possession; there refers to place/existence; they're means they are. Their books are there . They're ready. Replace they're with "they are" to test it. Your / You're Your shows possession. You're means you are. Is this your bag? You're early. Replace you're with "you are". Its / It's Its shows possession. It's means it is or it has. The company changed its policy. It's ready. Apostrophe means contraction, not possession. Desert / Dessert Desert can mean a dry region or abandon. Dessert is the sweet course after a meal. They crossed the desert . We ordered dessert . Dessert has two s letters. Elicit / Illicit Elicit means draw out a response. Illicit means illegal or forbidden. The question elicited a strong response. Illicit trade was reported. Elicit = obtain a response; illicit = unlawful.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 11 Words Difference Example Memory cue Emigrate / Immigrate Emigrate means leave one country to live elsewhere. Immigrate means enter another country to live there. They emigrated from India. They immigrated to Canada. From -> emigrate; to -> immigrate. Farther / Further Farther generally refers to physical distance. Further often refers to additional extent or figurative progress. The village is farther than expected. We need further discussion. Physical distance -> farther; additional -> further. Fewer / Less Fewer is used with countable plural nouns. Less is generally used with uncountable nouns. Fewer students were absent. We have less time. Countable -> fewer; uncountable -> less. Historic / Historical Historic means important in history. Historical means related to history. It was a historic decision. We studied historical records. Historic = significant; historical = connected with history. Lend / Borrow Lend means give something temporarily. Borrow means take/use temporarily with permission. Can you lend me a pen? May I borrow your pen? Direction matters: lender gives, borrower receives. Lie / Lay Lie means recline/rest. Lay means put something down and normally takes an object. I want to lie down. Lay the book on the table. Lay needs an object: lay the book. Wary / Weary Wary means cautious. Weary means tired. Be wary of scams. After the trip, she was weary . Wary -> caution; weary -> tiredness. How to solve a confused-word question \001 First decide what the sentence means. \001 Then identify whether the blank requires a noun, verb, adjective, adverb, etc. \001 Check the exact relation: possession, comparison, result, action, place, time, or legality. \001 Eliminate any option that is close in spelling but wrong in meaning. \001 Read the completed sentence once more for natural usage. Common examination trap The distractor is often a familiar word that is nearly correct. Do not choose an option because it "looks right". The difference must fit the sentence exactly.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 12 SECTION 2.3 - PHOBIAS (32) The term phobia is used in vocabulary questions for an intense fear or aversion associated with a specific object, activity, place, or situation. For examination purposes, learn the name, the thing feared, and the root that points to it. Root-based learning is useful. Once the root is recognised, an unfamiliar term becomes easier to decode. Phobia Fear / aversion related to Root cue Acrophobia heights acro = high Claustrophobia enclosed or confined spaces claustro = enclosed space Agoraphobia situations/places where escape or help may feel difficult agora = open/public place Arachnophobia spiders arachno = spider Hydrophobia water hydro = water Nyctophobia darkness/night nycto = night Glossophobia public speaking glosso = tongue/speech Xenophobia strangers/foreigners xeno = stranger/foreign Zoophobia animals zoo = animals Thanatophobia death thanato = death Astraphobia thunder/lightning astra = celestial phenomena Important distinction Phobia indicates fear. Mania indicates excessive preoccupation or an intense urge/obsession in the vocabulary sense. Do not interchange the two. Example question: Fear of heights is called acrophobia . The quickest route is to recognise acro = high .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 13 SECTION 2.4 - MANIAS (33) In vocabulary study, a mania refers to an excessive enthusiasm, preoccupation, or compulsive tendency connected with a particular activity or object. Learn the word together with the root and the central idea. Mania Meaning / preoccupation Root cue Bibliomania excessive passion for collecting or reading books biblio = books Kleptomania compulsive tendency to steal things klepto = steal Megalomania obsession with power, importance, or grandiosity megalo = great/large Dipsomania abnormal craving for alcohol dipso = alcohol Pyromania compulsive fascination with or urge to set fires pyro = fire Graphomania excessive desire to write grapho = writing Erotomania obsessive preoccupation involving romantic or sexual attraction eroto = love/desire Root strategy \001 biblio -> books -> bibliomania \001 pyro -> fire -> pyromania \001 klepto -> steal -> kleptomania \001 grapho -> writing -> graphomania Examination approach In a multiple-choice question, first identify the object or behaviour in the definition, then match it to the root. This is usually faster than trying to memorise the full word from spelling alone.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 14 SECTION 2.5 - PREFIXES & SUFFIXES (34-36) A prefix is added to the beginning of a word. A suffix is added to the end. They often change the meaning, grammatical category, or both. Example: un + happy = unhappy . Here un- changes the meaning to "not happy". happy + ness = happiness . Here -ness turns an adjective into a noun. Common Prefixes Prefix Usual meaning Examples un- not / opposite unfair, unhappy, uncertain dis- not / opposite / reversal disagree, disconnect, dishonest in- / im- / il- / ir- not inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular re- again rewrite, reconsider, rebuild pre- before preview, prepay, pretest post- after postgraduate, postwar anti- against antiwar, antibiotic, antisocial auto- self autobiography, automatic bi- two bicycle, bilingual tri- three triangle, tricycle mis- wrongly / badly misunderstand, mislead co- together / jointly cooperate, coauthor sub- under / below submarine, subconscious super- above / beyond superhuman, supermarket inter- between / among international, interact trans- across / beyond transport, transcontinental

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide Page 15 Common Suffixes Suffix Usual function / meaning Examples -ness state or quality; noun kindness, darkness, happiness -ment result/action; noun development, achievement -tion / -sion action/result; noun education, decision -er / -or person who does something teacher, actor -ful full of careful, useful, hopeful -less without careless, hopeless, fearless -able / -ible capable of being readable, visible -ous having the quality of dangerous, famous -ive having the nature of active, creative -ly usually forms an adverb quickly, carefully Negative prefixes: a key distinction The forms in-, im-, il-, ir- often mean "not", but the form changes according to spelling/sound patterns: impossible , illegal , irregular . Learn the examples as families rather than trying to infer every spelling mechanically. How to decode an unfamiliar word \001 Look at the beginning and identify a possible prefix. \001 Look at the ending and identify a possible suffix. \001 Use the base word to estimate the central meaning. \001 Combine the pieces and test the result against the sentence context. \001 Treat the result as a clue, not as an automatic dictionary definition.

title: MHT CET MBA Vocabulary Master Guide HINGLISH
contentSample: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS VOCABULARY MASTER GUIDE Hinglish Explanation + Examples + Exam Logic Vocabulary Syllabus Covered Section Topic 2.1 List of Words 2.2 Words Confused & Misused 2.3 Phobias 2.4 Manias 2.5 Prefixes & Suffixes 2.6 Analogies 2.7 Synonyms 2.8 Antonyms 2.9 One Word Substitution 2.10 Idioms / Phrases Study approach: Har word ko sirf ratna
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS VOCABULARY MASTER GUIDE Hinglish Explanation + Examples + Exam Logic Vocabulary Syllabus Covered Section Topic 2.1 List of Words 2.2 Words Confused & Misused 2.3 Phobias 2.4 Manias 2.5 Prefixes & Suffixes 2.6 Analogies 2.7 Synonyms 2.8 Antonyms 2.9 One Word Substitution 2.10 Idioms / Phrases Study approach: Har word ko sirf ratna nahi hai. Pehle meaning samjho, phir Hinglish idea banao, example dekho, related words compare karo aur finally MCQ mein use karo. The supplied syllabus image is used for the section structure and page ranges. The word banks and examples below are structured preparation material for those headings, not a verbatim reproduction of unseen source pages.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 2 SECTION 2.1 \001 LIST OF WORDS Is section ka purpose: Ye tumhara basic vocabulary bank build karta hai. Exam mein word ka meaning, context, synonym, antonym ya correct usage poocha ja sakta hai. Ek word ko kaise padhna hai? \001 Word: exact spelling yaad karo. \001 Meaning: ek simple English meaning samjho. \001 Hinglish: apni language mein concept pakdo. \001 Example: sentence mein word ka use dekho. \001 Synonym/Antonym: related words connect karo. \001 Trap: similar-looking word se confuse mat ho. Word families: Ek base word ke different forms ko saath mein learn karne se memorisation kam hota hai. Base Noun Adjective Verb Adverb success success successful succeed successfully decision decision decisive decide decisively beauty beauty beautiful beautify beautifully danger danger dangerous endanger dangerously Important words Word Meaning Hinglish Example Syn. Ant. Exam trap Abundant Large quantity mein available bahut zyada matra mein The district has abundant rainfall. plentiful scarce Sufficient ka exact meaning nahi; abundant = large amount. Adverse Unfavourable / harmful pratikool ya nuksan pahunchane wala The project faced adverse weather conditions. unfavourable favourable Conditions/things ke liye common; person ke liye usually averse. Alleviate Make less severe problem/dard ko kam karna The policy may alleviate pressure. relieve aggravate Completely remove nahi; severity kam karna. Ambiguous More than one possible meaning meaning clear nahi, multiple interpretations possible The statement was ambiguous. unclear unambiguous Difficult ka synonym nahi. Benevolent Kind and helpful dayalu aur bhalaai karne wala The benevolent donor supported the school. kind malevolent Goodwill aur kindness par focus. Candid Honest and straightforward seedha aur imaandaar She gave a candid opinion. frank evasive Rude hona zaroori nahi. Coherent Logical and well connected ideas logically connected His explanation was coherent. logical incoherent Ideas ka connection important hai. Conspicuous Very noticeable jo easily notice ho jaye The bright sign was conspicuous. noticeable inconspicuous Noticeable ka meaning; attractive zaroori nahi. Diligent Steady and careful effort mehnati aur consistently careful The diligent student revised daily. industrious negligent Intelligence nahi, consistent effort. Eloquent Fluent and persuasive expression achhi aur prabhavshali expression The speaker gave an eloquent address. articulate inarticulate Speaking/writing ki effective expression. Frugal Careful with money/resources paise/resources soch-samajhkar use karna She is frugal with money. thrifty wasteful Frugal positive quality ho sakti hai; miserly alag hai. Imminent Likely very soon bahut jaldi hone wala A severe storm is imminent. impending remote Soon hone wali event. Meticulous Very careful about details har detail ko bahut dhyan se dekhna He is meticulous about records. thorough careless Small details par special attention. Obsolete No longer in use purana aur ab use mein nahi The machine became obsolete. outdated current Usually replaced/no longer useful in context. Pragmatic Practical and result-focused practical aur workable result par focus She took a pragmatic approach. practical impractical Jo reality mein kaam kare. Reluctant Unwilling or hesitant mann na hona / hesitant hona He was reluctant to accept. unwilling eager Unable nahi; willing nahi ya hesitation. Scrutinise Examine very carefully bahut dhyan se jaanchna The auditor scrutinised the records. examine overlook Simply look at se stronger. Vigilant Watchful and alert satark aur alert Security staff remained vigilant. alert careless Continuous alertness. Viable Capable of working successfully practically kaam kar sakta hai They proposed a viable model. feasible unworkable Plans/options/systems ke liye common. Wary Cautious because of possible danger savdhan rehna Be wary of suspicious messages. cautious trusting Wary = cautious; weary = tired.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 3 SECTION 2.2 \001 WORDS CONFUSED & MISUSED Ye words spelling ya sound mein similar hote hain, isliye exam mein easily trap bana sakte hain. Best method: meaning + grammar role + sentence teenon check karo. Pair Difference Example Memory cue Affect / Effect Affect usually verb = influence; Effect usually noun = result. Lack of sleep affects concentration. / The effect was visible. Affect \002 action; Effect \002 result. Accept / Except Accept = receive/agree; Except = excluding. She accepted the offer. / Everyone came except Arjun. Receive/agree vs leave out. Advice / Advise Advice = noun; Advise = verb. He gave advice. / I advise you to revise. Advice = thing; Advise = action. Principal / Principle Principal = school head / main; Principle = rule/belief. The principal spoke. / Honesty is a principle. Principal \002 person/main; Principle \002 rule. Compliment / Complement Compliment = praise; Complement = complete/fit well. She complimented me. / The colour complements the design. Praise vs complete/fit. Stationary / Stationery Stationary = not moving; Stationery = writing material. The car was stationary. / I bought stationery. Stationary = still; Stationery = writing. Loose / Lose Loose = not tight; Lose = misplace/fail to win. The belt is loose. / Don't lose hope. Loose has double o. Then / Than Then = time/sequence; Than = comparison. Study then revise. / Taller than me. Time vs comparison. Their / There / They're Their = possession; There = place/existence; They're = they are. Their books are there. They're ready. Try replacing they're with they are. Your / You're Your = possession; You're = you are. Your bag. / You're early. Replace you're with you are. Its / It's Its = possession; It's = it is/it has. The company changed its policy. / It's ready. Apostrophe = contraction. Desert / Dessert Desert = dry region/abandon; Dessert = sweet course. They crossed the desert. / We ordered dessert. Dessert has two s. Elicit / Illicit Elicit = draw out response; Illicit = illegal. The question elicited a response. / Illicit trade. Response vs unlawful. Emigrate / Immigrate Emigrate = leave country; Immigrate = enter country. They emigrated from India. / They immigrated to Canada. From \002 emigrate; to \002 immigrate. Farther / Further Farther = physical distance; Further = additional/figurative. The village is farther. / Further discussion is needed. Distance vs additional. Fewer / Less Fewer + countable plural; Less + uncountable. Fewer students. / Less time. Countable vs uncountable. Historic / Historical Historic = important in history; Historical = related to history. A historic decision. / Historical records. Significant vs history-related. Lend / Borrow Lend = give temporarily; Borrow = take temporarily. Lend me a pen. / May I borrow it? Direction matters. Lie / Lay Lie = recline/rest; Lay = put something down and takes object. I want to lie down. / Lay the book here. Lay needs an object. Wary / Weary Wary = cautious; Weary = tired. Be wary of scams. / She was weary after travel. Caution vs tiredness. Question-solving method \001 Sentence ka exact meaning samjho. \001 Blank ko noun/verb/adjective etc. kya chahiye, check karo. \001 Meaning relation check karo: possession, result, comparison, place, time, legality etc. \001 Sirf spelling dekhkar answer mat choose karo. \001 Completed sentence ko ek baar naturally read karo.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 4 SECTION 2.3 \001 PHOBIAS Vocabulary mein phobia ka use intense fear ya strong aversion ke sense mein hota hai. Exam ke liye teen cheezein yaad rakho: term + fear + root . Phobia Fear / aversion Root cue Acrophobia Heights acro = high Claustrophobia Enclosed/confined spaces claustro = enclosed Agoraphobia Situations/places where escape or help may feel difficult agora = open/public place Arachnophobia Spiders arachno = spider Hydrophobia Water hydro = water Nyctophobia Darkness/night nycto = night Glossophobia Public speaking glosso = tongue/speech Xenophobia Strangers/foreigners xeno = stranger/foreign Zoophobia Animals zoo = animals Thanatophobia Death thanato = death Astraphobia Thunder/lightning astra = celestial phenomena Core distinction: Phobia = fear/aversion. Mania = excessive preoccupation/urge. Dono ko mix mat karo.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 5 SECTION 2.4 \001 MANIAS Vocabulary context mein mania ka meaning excessive enthusiasm, strong preoccupation, ya compulsive tendency ho sakta hai. Root ko identify karna MCQ mein fast method hai. Term Meaning Root cue Bibliomania Books ke saath excessive passion/preoccupation biblio = books Kleptomania Things steal karne ki compulsive tendency klepto = steal Megalomania Power, importance ya grandiosity ka obsession megalo = great/large Dipsomania Alcohol ki abnormal craving dipso = alcohol Pyromania Fire set karne ki compulsive fascination/urge pyro = fire Graphomania Excessive desire to write grapho = writing Erotomania Romantic/sexual attraction se related obsessive preoccupation eroto = love/desire Fast recall: biblio \002 books \002 bibliomania; pyro \002 fire \002 pyromania; klepto \002 steal \002 kleptomania; grapho \002 writing \002 graphomania.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 6 SECTION 2.5 \001 PREFIXES & SUFFIXES Prefix word ke beginning mein add hota hai. Suffix word ke end mein add hota hai. Example: un + happy = unhappy \002 un- meaning 'not'. happy + ness = happiness \002 -ness quality/state ka noun banata hai. Common Prefixes Prefix Meaning Examples un- not/opposite unfair, unhappy, uncertain dis- not/opposite/reversal disagree, disconnect, dishonest in-/im-/il-/ir- not inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular re- again rewrite, reconsider, rebuild pre- before preview, prepay, pretest post- after postgraduate, postwar anti- against antiwar, antibiotic, antisocial auto- self autobiography, automatic bi- two bicycle, bilingual tri- three triangle, tricycle mis- wrongly/badly misunderstand, mislead co- together/jointly cooperate, coauthor sub- under/below submarine, subconscious super- above/beyond superhuman, supermarket inter- between/among international, interact trans- across/beyond transport, transcontinental Common Suffixes Suffix Meaning/function Examples -ness state/quality; noun kindness, darkness, happiness -ment result/action; noun development, achievement -tion / -sion action/result; noun education, decision -er / -or person who does something teacher, actor -ful full of careful, useful, hopeful -less without careless, hopeless, fearless -able / -ible capable of being readable, visible -ous having the quality of dangerous, famous -ive having the nature of active, creative -ly usually forms an adverb quickly, carefully Unfamiliar word ko decode kaise karein? \001 Beginning dekho: koi prefix hai? \001 Ending dekho: koi suffix hai?

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 7 \001 Base word identify karo. \001 Pieces ko combine karke rough meaning banao. \001 Sentence context se verify karo. Prefix/suffix clue hai, guaranteed dictionary definition nahi.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 8 SECTION 2.6 \001 ANALOGIES Analogy mein main kaam words ko individually dekhna nahi, balki relationship identify karna hai. A : B :: C : ? ka matlab hai: A ka B ke saath jo relation hai, wahi C ka answer ke saath hona chahiye. Relationship Example Meaning Synonym rapid : fast :: tiny : small Dono words nearly same meaning. Antonym hot : cold :: success : failure Opposite relationship. Worker : workplace doctor : hospital :: judge : court Person ka workplace. Worker : tool carpenter : saw :: writer : pen Person ka tool. Object : function knife : cut :: pen : write Object ka function. Animal : sound dog : bark :: cat : meow Animal ki characteristic sound. Part : whole wheel : car :: page : book Part belongs to whole. Young : adult calf : cow :: puppy : dog Young form \002 adult. Material : product gold : jewellery :: wood : furniture Material se product. Cause : effect exercise : fitness :: study : knowledge First contributes to second. Degree/intensity warm : hot :: cool : cold Intensity relation. Analogy solve karne ke 4 steps \001 First pair ka relation ek complete sentence mein bolo: 'Doctor works in hospital.' \001 Same sentence structure second pair par apply karo. \001 Har option ko same relationship se test karo. \001 Sirf related word dekhkar answer mat choose karo; exact relationship same hona chahiye.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 9 SECTION 2.7 \001 SYNONYMS Synonym ka matlab hai same ya closely related meaning . Perfect synonym har sentence mein possible nahi hota, isliye context important hai. Example: rapid \002 fast. Lekin synonym question mein best answer wahi hoga jo sentence ke meaning aur tone dono ko fit kare. Word Useful synonyms Abandon leave, desert, forsake Abundant plentiful, ample, copious Accurate correct, precise, exact Brief short, concise, succinct Cautious careful, wary, prudent Commence begin, start, initiate Conceal hide, cover, disguise Conspicuous noticeable, prominent, obvious Diminish reduce, decrease, lessen Diligent industrious, hardworking, assiduous Evident clear, obvious, apparent Fragile delicate, breakable, vulnerable Generous liberal, charitable, magnanimous Hostile unfriendly, antagonistic, aggressive Impartial fair, unbiased, neutral Imminent impending, near, approaching Lucid clear, intelligible, comprehensible Meticulous careful, painstaking, thorough Obsolete outdated, antiquated, outmoded Pragmatic practical, realistic, sensible Reluctant unwilling, hesitant, disinclined Resilient strong, adaptable, tough Scrutinise examine, inspect, investigate Vague unclear, imprecise, indefinite Vigilant alert, watchful, attentive Viable feasible, workable, practicable Synonym question ka method \001 Context diya hai to sentence pehle padho. \001 Options dekhne se pehle rough meaning mind mein lao. \001 Pehle obvious antonyms eliminate karo. \001 Remaining options mein exact meaning aur tone compare karo. \001 Sirf related word ko synonym mat samjho.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 10 SECTION 2.8 \001 ANTONYMS Antonym ka matlab opposite ya contrasting meaning. Har opposite same type ka nahi hota. Type Meaning Example Binary Do contrasting states mein se ek alive \003 dead Gradable Scale par opposite ends hot \003 cold Relational Opposite relationships buy \003 sell Directional Opposite movement/direction advance \003 retreat Word Antonym Abundant scarce Ancient modern Artificial natural Expand contract Permanent temporary Optimistic pessimistic Generous stingy Hostile friendly Victory defeat Transparent opaque Superior inferior Maximum minimum Include exclude Encourage discourage Reveal conceal Create destroy Accept reject Flexible rigid Complex simple Frequent rare Vivid dull Mandatory optional Reluctant eager Visible hidden Genuine fake Context trap: 'Light' ka opposite weight ke context mein heavy ho sakta hai, aur brightness ke context mein dark . Isliye exact sense identify karo.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 11 SECTION 2.9 \001 ONE WORD SUBSTITUTION Ek complete phrase/description ko ek precise word se replace karna = One Word Substitution. Description One word Memory cue One who loves books Bibliophile biblio = books One who hates mankind Misanthrope mis = dislike, anthro = human One who loves mankind Philanthropist philo = love, anthro = human One who knows many languages Polyglot poly = many, glot = language One who studies mankind Anthropologist study of humans One who studies plants Botanist botany = plants One who studies animals Zoologist zoology = animals One who cannot read/write Illiterate literate = able to read/write One who speaks very little Taciturn reserved/sparing in speech One who believes in God Theist belief in God One who does not believe in God Atheist absence of belief in God One who believes in one God Monotheist mono = one One who believes in many gods Polytheist poly = many One who is neutral/non-partisan Impartial not taking sides Place where books are kept Library books Place where aircraft are kept Hangar aircraft Place where coins are made Mint coins Place where dead bodies are kept for examination Morgue dead bodies Place where animals are kept for public viewing Zoo animals Happening once a year Annual yearly Happening twice a year Biannual twice a year Happening every two years Biennial once in two years A person who collects stamps Philatelist stamps A person who collects coins Numismatist coins Government by the people Democracy people rule Government by a king/queen Monarchy monarch Place for scientific experiments Laboratory experiments Person who writes dictionaries Lexicographer dictionary writer Person who writes about own life Autobiographer own life Person who travels place to place Itinerant travels from place to place Important: Biannual = twice a year. Biennial = once every two years. Dono ko confuse mat karo. Solve karte waqt pehle identify karo: person? place? belief? habit? time? process? Phir exact definition match karo.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 12 SECTION 2.10 \001 IDIOMS / PHRASES Idiom ek fixed expression hai jiska actual meaning words ke literal meaning se different ho sakta hai. Idiom ko ek complete unit ki tarah learn karo. Idiom / Phrase Actual meaning Break the ice Start a friendly conversation / awkwardness reduce karna Once in a blue moon Very rarely A blessing in disguise Jo initially bad lage but later beneficial prove ho Hit the nail on the head Exactly right thing kehna/karna Spill the beans Secret reveal karna Beat around the bush Main point avoid karna Cost an arm and a leg Bahut expensive hona Under the weather Unwell feel karna Call it a day Aaj ka work stop karna In hot water Trouble mein hona Piece of cake Very easy Burn the midnight oil Late night work/study karna At the eleventh hour Last possible moment A storm in a teacup Small issue par large reaction By leaps and bounds Very rapidly Keep an eye on Watch/monitor karna Make both ends meet Available income mein manage karna On cloud nine Extremely happy Add fuel to the fire Bad situation ko worse banana Bite the bullet Difficult situation courage se face karna Read between the lines Hidden/implied meaning samajhna In the long run Long period ke baad/over a long period On the same page Same understanding hona A double-edged sword Advantages aur disadvantages dono hona The tip of the iceberg Large issue ka sirf small visible part Go the extra mile Extra effort karna Take with a grain of salt Completely true maan kar accept na karna Get cold feet Planned action se pehle nervous ho jana Pull strings Influence use karke result lena Turn a blind eye Jaan-bujhkar ignore karna Cut corners Steps skip karke cheaply/carelessly kaam karna Through thick and thin Good and bad times mein In black and white Written/clear form mein At loggerheads Strong disagreement mein In the nick of time Too late hone se just pehle By word of mouth Spoken communication se

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 13 Idiom / Phrase Actual meaning Keep at bay Door/prevent karke rakhna Put off Postpone karna Look into Investigate karna Look after Take care of karna Give up Quit/stop karna Carry out Perform/complete karna Bring up Topic mention/raise karna Put up with Tolerate karna

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 14 IDIOMS \001 HOW TO REMEMBER Literal translation se idioms yaad karna difficult ho sakta hai. Better method hai expression ko ek situation se connect karna. Idiom Situation memory Break the ice New group mein sab silent hain. Tum joke bolte ho aur conversation start hoti hai \002 break the ice. Spill the beans Kisi ne secret bata diya \002 spill the beans. Bite the bullet Difficult task avoid karne ke bajay courage se karna \002 bite the bullet. Burn the midnight oil Exam ke liye raat tak padhna \002 burn the midnight oil. Literal vs actual meaning Expression Literal reading Actual meaning Break the ice Frozen ice todna Friendly interaction start karna Spill the beans Beans gira dena Secret reveal karna Bite the bullet Bullet ko bite karna Difficult situation bravely face karna Under the weather Weather ke neeche hona Unwell feel karna

MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary Master Guide \001 Page 15 VOCABULARY REVISION SYSTEM Vocabulary ka best revision sirf rereading nahi hai. Book close karke meaning recall karna zyada useful hai. Stage What to do Read 10\00415 new items meaning + one example ke saath padho. Recall Notes band karke meaning bolo. Compare Confused pairs, synonyms aur antonyms compare karo. Apply 5\00410 MCQs solve karo. Revisit Same items ko 1 day, 3 days aur 7 days baad recall karo. Topic-wise method Topic Best method List of Words Word + meaning + context + related words Confused & Misused Pair banao + dono ke separate sentences Phobias Root \002 fear Manias Root \002 obsession/behaviour Prefixes & Suffixes Word ko parts mein break karo Analogies Relationship ko complete sentence mein bolo Synonyms Synonym families + context Antonyms Contrast pairs One Word Substitution People/places/beliefs/time categories Idioms/Phrases Idiom ko real-life situation se connect karo Daily vocabulary routine \001 10\00415 new words: meaning + Hinglish + example. \001 5 confused words: pair-wise revision. \001 5 synonyms + 5 antonyms: active recall. \001 5 one-word substitutions: phrase dekhkar word recall. \001 5 idioms: meaning + one situation. \001 5 MCQs: same-day application.

contentSample: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary - Summary + Extended Analogies TASK 1 - Learning Pack | Hinglish explanations | Based on the supplied vocabulary syllabus headings Use this first: This PDF is for understanding and revising Vocabulary before testing. The actual question paper/mock can be kept English-only later; here the explanations are intentionally Hinglish so the concepts become easier to remember. 1
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary - Summary + Extended Analogies TASK 1 - Learning Pack | Hinglish explanations | Based on the supplied vocabulary syllabus headings Use this first: This PDF is for understanding and revising Vocabulary before testing. The actual question paper/mock can be kept English-only later; here the explanations are intentionally Hinglish so the concepts become easier to remember. 1. What You Need to Cover Your supplied syllabus image lists these 10 vocabulary areas: List of Words; Words Confused & Misused; Phobias; Manias; Prefixes & Suffixes; Analogies; Synonyms; Antonyms; One Word Substitution; Idioms/Phrases. The image gives the section headings and page ranges, but it does not show the full word lists. So the examples below are a structured exam-prep learning set built around those headings, not a claim that every example appears verbatim on those pages. 2. List of Words - How to Learn a New Word Best pattern: Word -> simple meaning -> Hinglish meaning -> example -> synonym -> antonym -> common trap. Word Meaning Hinglish Example Abundant More than enough Bahut zyada / plenty The region has abundant rainfall. Adverse Unfavourable / harmful Nuksaan pahunchane wala The match was cancelled due to adverse weather. Alleviate Reduce pain or difficulty Problem/pain kam karna The medicine helped alleviate the pain. Ambiguous Having more than one possible meaning Meaning clear na ho The sentence is ambiguous. Benevolent Kind and generous Dayalu aur helpful A benevolent donor funded the library. Candid Honest and direct Seedha aur honest She gave a candid opinion. Coherent Logical and well connected Baat logically connected ho His explanation was coherent. Conspicuous Easy to notice Jo clearly notice ho The red bag was conspicuous. Diligent Hard-working and careful Mehnati aur careful She is a diligent student. Eloquent Fluent and persuasive in speech Achhe tareeke se bolne wala He gave an eloquent speech. Frugal Careful with money Paise soch-samajhkar kharch karna He is frugal, not miserly. Imminent About to happen Bahut jaldi hone wala A storm is imminent. Meticulous Very careful about details Har detail ka bahut dhyan rakhna She is meticulous about records. Obsolete No longer useful or in use Purana aur practically use se bahar The machine is obsolete. Pragmatic Practical and realistic Practical soch wala We need a pragmatic solution. Reluctant Unwilling / hesitant Mann na hote hue He was reluctant to speak. Scrutinise Examine closely Bahut dhyan se check karna Please scrutinise the document. Vigilant Watchful and alert Chaukanna rehna Security staff remained vigilant.

Word Meaning Hinglish Example Viable Capable of working successfully Jo practically kaam kar sake We need a viable plan. Wary Cautious because of possible danger Savdhaan / cautious Be wary of unknown links. 3. Words Confused & Misused Yahan biggest trap ye hota hai ki words similar sound/looks karte hain, but meaning ya grammar role different hota hai. Pair Difference Examples Affect / Effect Affect usually verb; effect usually noun. Stress can affect health. / The effect was immediate. Accept / Except Accept = receive/agree; except = excluding. I accept the offer. / Everyone came except Ravi. Advice / Advise Advice = noun; advise = verb. Good advice helps. / I advise you to revise. Principal / Principle Principal = head/main; principle = rule/belief. The principal arrived. / Honesty is a principle. Stationary / Stationery Stationary = not moving; stationery = writing materials. The car was stationary. / Buy some stationery. Compliment / Complement Compliment = praise; complement = complete/match. She complimented me. / The tie complements the shirt. Loose / Lose Loose = not tight; lose = fail to keep. This shirt is loose. / Do not lose your notes. Then / Than Then = time/result; than = comparison. Finish, then rest. / She is taller than me. Their / There / They're Possession / place / they are. Their books are there. / They're ready. Your / You're Possession / you are. Your bag is here. / You're late. Its / It's Possession / it is. The dog wagged its tail. / It's raining. Desert / Dessert Desert = dry region; dessert = sweet course. They crossed the desert. / We had dessert. Elicit / Illicit Elicit = draw out a response; illicit = illegal. The question elicited laughter. / Illicit trade is banned. Farther / Further Farther often physical distance; further often additional degree/discussion. The station is farther away. / For further details, call us. Fewer / Less Fewer with countable nouns; less with uncountable quantities. Fewer students came. / Less water was needed. Lie / Lay Lie = recline; lay = put something down. I will lie down. / Lay the book on the table. Wary / Weary Wary = cautious; weary = tired. Be wary of scams. / She felt weary after work. 4. Phobias Memory rule: Phobia = strong fear/aversion connected to a specific thing or situation. Term Fear of Memory cue / example Acrophobia Heights Acro -> high. He avoids tall buildings. Claustrophobia Enclosed/tight spaces Closed lift makes him uncomfortable.

Term Fear of Memory cue / example Agoraphobia Certain open/public situations or places where escape may feel difficult Crowded/public settings can trigger fear. Arachnophobia Spiders Arachno -> spider. Hydrophobia Water Hydro -> water. Xenophobia Strangers/foreigners Xeno -> foreign/strange. Nyctophobia Darkness/night Nycto -> night. Glossophobia Public speaking Gloss -> tongue/speech association. Zoophobia Animals Zoo -> animals. Thanatophobia Death Thanato -> death. Astraphobia Thunder/lightning Astro -> stars/sky; remember storm fear. 5. Manias Mania: an unusually strong or excessive preoccupation/obsessive tendency toward something. For CET-style vocabulary, focus on the root + meaning. Term Associated with Memory cue / example Bibliomania Books Biblio -> books. Strong obsession with collecting books. Kleptomania Stealing Klepto -> stealing. An urge to steal objects. Megalomania Power/grandeur Mega -> great/big. Inflated belief in one's importance/power. Dipsomania Alcohol Dipso -> alcohol-related term. Pyromania Fire Pyro -> fire. Strong fascination/urge involving fire-setting. Graphomania Writing Grapho -> writing. Excessive urge to write. Erotomania Erotic/love-related delusion or obsession Eroto -> erotic/love-related. 6. Prefixes & Suffixes Prefixes - meaning at the beginning Prefix Meaning Examples un- not/reverse unhappy, unfair, unlock dis- not/opposite/separation disagree, dishonest, disconnect in-/im-/il-/ir- not inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular re- again/back rewrite, rebuild, reconsider pre- before preview, prepay, prehistoric post- after postwar, postgraduate, post-test anti- against antiwar, antivirus, antisocial auto- self automatic, autobiography bi- two bilingual, bicycle tri- three triangle, trilingual

Prefix Meaning Examples mis- wrong/badly misunderstand, mislead, misuse co- together/with cooperate, coexist, coauthor sub- under/below subway, subconscious, substandard super- above/beyond superhuman, supermarket, supersede inter- between/among international, interact trans- across/beyond transport, transfer, transnational Suffixes - meaning/function added at the end Suffix Typical function Examples -ness Forms noun of state/quality kindness, darkness, happiness -ment Forms noun/action/result development, movement, agreement -tion / -sion Forms nouns creation, decision, expansion -er / -or Person who does teacher, actor, inventor -ful Full of helpful, careful, useful -less Without careless, hopeless, fearless -able / -ible Capable of being readable, visible, flexible -ous Having the quality of dangerous, famous, curious -ive Having a quality/related to active, effective, creative -ly Often forms adverbs quickly, carefully, clearly 7. Synonyms - Same or Nearly Same Meaning Exam mein exact dictionary-perfect equality zaroori nahi hoti. Context ke according closest meaning choose karo. Word Useful synonym Quick example Abandon Leave / desert He abandoned the plan. Accurate Correct / precise The answer is accurate. Brief Short Give a brief reply. Cautious Wary / careful Be cautious online. Commence Begin / start The meeting commenced at noon. Conceal Hide He concealed the evidence. Diminish Reduce / decrease The noise diminished. Evident Clear / obvious The mistake was evident. Fragile Delicate Handle the glass; it is fragile. Generous Liberal / giving She was generous with her time. Hostile Unfriendly / antagonistic The crowd became hostile. Impartial Unbiased / neutral A judge should be impartial. Lucid Clear / easy to understand Her explanation was lucid. Obsolete Outdated The software is obsolete. Resilient Able to recover The team remained resilient.

Word Useful synonym Quick example Vague Unclear / indefinite His reply was vague. Vigilant Alert / watchful Security must stay vigilant. Viable Practical / workable That is a viable option. 8. Antonyms - Opposite Meaning Word Antonym Example pair Abundant Scarce abundant resources / scarce resources Ancient Modern ancient temple / modern building Artificial Natural artificial light / natural light Expand Contract business expands / market contracts Permanent Temporary permanent job / temporary arrangement Optimistic Pessimistic optimistic view / pessimistic view Generous Stingy generous donor / stingy person Hostile Friendly hostile response / friendly response Victory Defeat victory / defeat Transparent Opaque transparent glass / opaque glass Superior Inferior superior quality / inferior quality Maximum Minimum maximum value / minimum value Include Exclude include all / exclude one Encourage Discourage encourage effort / discourage effort Reveal Conceal reveal a secret / conceal a secret Flexible Rigid flexible rule / rigid rule Complex Simple complex system / simple system Frequent Rare frequent visits / rare visits Vivid Dull vivid memory / dull image Reluctant Eager reluctant to go / eager to go 9. One Word Substitution Description One word Meaning / cue A person who loves books Bibliophile Biblio = books A person who hates mankind Misanthrope Misanthro = dislike of people A person who helps humanity Philanthropist Philanthro = love of humanity A person who knows many languages Polyglot Poly = many; glot = language Study of humans Anthropology Anthropo = human Study of plants Botany Plant science Study of animals Zoology Zoo = animals Unable to read or write Illiterate Literacy absent One who speaks very little Taciturn Reserved/silent

Description One word Meaning / cue Believer in God Theist Theism = belief in God One who does not believe in God Atheist A-theist Believer in one God Monotheist Mono = one Believer in many gods Polytheist Poly = many Not taking sides Impartial Unbiased Place where aircraft are kept Hangar Not hanger Place where dead bodies are kept Morgue Hospital/legal setting A person who collects stamps Philatelist Stamp collector A person who collects coins Numismatist Coin collector Government by the people Democracy Demo = people Government by a king/queen Monarchy Mono = one ruler 10. Idioms / Phrases Idioms ko literal meaning se mat solve karo. Sentence ka overall situation dekho. Idiom Meaning Example Break the ice Start a friendly interaction A joke helped break the ice. Once in a blue moon Very rarely He visits us once in a blue moon. A blessing in disguise Something that seems bad but turns out useful Missing that train was a blessing in disguise. Hit the nail on the head Describe something exactly You hit the nail on the head. Spill the beans Reveal a secret She spilled the beans about the plan. Beat around the bush Avoid the main point Stop beating around the bush. Under the weather Feeling unwell I am under the weather today. Call it a day Stop working Let's call it a day. In hot water In trouble He is in hot water after the mistake. Piece of cake Very easy The first question was a piece of cake. Burn the midnight oil Work/study late at night She burned the midnight oil before the exam. At the eleventh hour At the last moment He submitted the form at the eleventh hour. By leaps and bounds Very rapidly Her English improved by leaps and bounds. Keep an eye on Watch carefully Keep an eye on the timer. Make both ends meet Manage expenses with income They struggle to make both ends meet. On cloud nine Extremely happy She was on cloud nine after the result. Add fuel to the fire Make a bad situation worse His comment added fuel to the fire. Bite the bullet Face a difficult situation bravely She bit the bullet and took the test. Read between the lines Understand hidden meaning Read between the lines of the email. Go the extra mile Make extra effort He went the extra mile to help the team. Take with a grain of salt Do not accept fully without questioning Take online rumours with a grain of salt.

Idiom Meaning Example Get cold feet Become nervous and back out He got cold feet before the presentation. Pull strings Use influence to get something done She pulled strings to arrange the meeting. Turn a blind eye Ignore deliberately The guard turned a blind eye to the issue. Cut corners Do something cheaply/easily by skipping proper steps Do not cut corners in preparation. 11. ANALOGIES - EXTENDED VERSION Core idea: A:B :: C:? means the relationship between A and B should be the same as the relationship between C and the answer. Do not match just because the words 'look related'. First identify the exact relationship. A. Synonym Analogy Question Answer Why Happy : Joyful :: Angry : ? Furious Joyful is a synonym of happy; furious is a synonym of angry. Begin : Commence :: End : ? Terminate Both are synonym pairs. Big : Large :: Small : ? Tiny Meaning relation is synonym. Quick : Rapid :: Silent : ? Quiet Same-meaning relation. Honest : Candid :: Watchful : ? Vigilant Candid ~ honest; vigilant ~ watchful. B. Antonym Analogy Question Answer Why Hot : Cold :: Up : ? Down Opposite relation. Victory : Defeat :: Accept : ? Reject Opposite relation. Expand : Contract :: Include : ? Exclude Opposites. Ancient : Modern :: Permanent : ? Temporary Opposite relation. Generous : Stingy :: Eager : ? Reluctant Opposite meaning. C. Person and Workplace Question Answer Why Teacher : School :: Doctor : ? Hospital Person usually works in that place. Judge : Court :: Chef : ? Kitchen Professional and workplace. Pilot : Cockpit :: Sailor : ? Ship Professional working environment. Librarian : Library :: Curator : ? Museum Person and institution/place. Mechanic : Garage :: Scientist : ? Laboratory Occupation and workplace. D. Person and Tool/Instrument Question Answer Why Writer : Pen :: Painter : ? Brush Tool used by the person. Carpenter : Saw :: Barber : ? Scissors Instrument used in the job. Surgeon : Scalpel :: Tailor : ? Needle Professional and instrument.

Question Answer Why Photographer : Camera :: Musician : ? Instrument Main working tool. Farmer : Plough :: Carpenter : ? Hammer Occupational tool relation. E. Object and Function Question Answer Why Knife : Cut :: Pen : ? Write Object and main function. Thermometer : Measure temperature :: Clock : ? Tell time Instrument and function. Refrigerator : Cool :: Heater : ? Heat Device and purpose. Key : Unlock :: Eraser : ? Erase Object and action. Camera : Photograph :: Microscope : ? Magnify/observe Instrument and function. F. Part and Whole Question Answer Why Wheel : Car :: Page : ? Book Part belongs to whole. Finger : Hand :: Toe : ? Foot Part-whole relation. Petal : Flower :: Leaf : ? Plant Component of a whole. Engine : Car :: Heart : ? Body Important internal part of whole. Chapter : Book :: Scene : ? Play Structural part of whole. G. Animal and Sound Question Answer Why Dog : Bark :: Cat : ? Meow Animal and characteristic sound. Horse : Neigh :: Cow : ? Moo Animal and sound. Lion : Roar :: Snake : ? Hiss Animal and sound. Crow : Caw :: Duck : ? Quack Animal and sound. Bee : Buzz :: Donkey : ? Bray Characteristic sound. H. Young One and Adult Question Answer Why Puppy : Dog :: Kitten : ? Cat Young one to adult animal. Calf : Cow :: Foal : ? Horse Young animal and adult. Lamb : Sheep :: Kid : ? Goat Young one relation. Cub : Lion :: Fawn : ? Deer Young one to adult. Chick : Hen :: Duckling : ? Duck Young one relation. I. Material and Product Question Answer Why Wood : Furniture :: Leather : ? Shoes Material used to make product. Gold : Jewellery :: Clay : ? Pottery Material and product. Wool : Sweater :: Cotton : ? Shirt Raw material and common product.

Question Answer Why Steel : Utensil :: Glass : ? Bottle Material-product relation. Flour : Bread :: Milk : ? Cheese Material/ingredient to product. J. Cause and Effect Question Answer Why Study : Knowledge :: Exercise : ? Fitness Activity leads to result. Rain : Flood :: Fire : ? Smoke Cause and effect. Neglect : Failure :: Practice : ? Improvement Action and outcome. Friction : Heat :: Pressure : ? Compression Cause produces effect. Hard work : Success :: Carelessness : ? Failure Likely consequence relation. K. Degree / Intensity Question Answer Why Warm : Hot :: Cool : ? Cold Increasing intensity along a scale. Annoyed : Angry :: Interested : ? Fascinated Degree/intensity increases. Drizzle : Rain :: Breeze : ? Wind Stronger degree of the same phenomenon. Whisper : Speak :: Sprint : ? Run Lower vs higher intensity/speed. Like : Love :: Dislike : ? Hate Increasing strength of feeling. L. Object and Place Question Answer Why Books : Library :: Animals : ? Zoo Objects/subjects and place where kept/seen. Aircraft : Hangar :: Ships : ? Harbour Vehicle and storage/berthing place. Art : Gallery :: Historical objects : ? Museum Things and public display place. Patients : Hospital :: Students : ? School People and institution. Money : Bank :: Prisoners : ? Jail Thing/person and place associated with it. M. Profession and Product Question Answer Why Author : Book :: Composer : ? Music Professional produces that work. Architect : Building :: Tailor : ? Clothes Professional creates product. Director : Film :: Painter : ? Painting Creator and creation. Chef : Meal :: Potter : ? Pot Person and product. Poet : Poem :: Sculptor : ? Sculpture Creator and creation. N. Group / Collection Question Answer Why Stars : Galaxy :: Trees : ? Forest Group/collection. Books : Library :: Animals : ? Zoo Collection/group in a place.

Question Answer Why Ships : Fleet :: Soldiers : ? Army Collective group. Players : Team :: Musicians : ? Band Group of members. Keys : Bunch :: Flowers : ? Bouquet Collection/group. O. Study / Field Relation Question Answer Why Plants : Botany :: Animals : ? Zoology Field of study. Stars : Astronomy :: Earthquake : ? Seismology Subject and scientific field. Mind : Psychology :: Society : ? Sociology Subject and discipline. Language : Linguistics :: Words/lexicon : ? Lexicography Language-related study/work. Ancient remains : Archaeology :: Fossils : ? Palaeontology Subject and field. P. Tool and Material Question Answer Why Pen : Ink :: Car : ? Fuel Tool/device operates using material. Lamp : Electricity :: Candle : ? Wax Object and material/source. Engine : Petrol :: Laptop : ? Battery/Power Device and energy source. Fireplace : Wood :: Stove : ? Gas Appliance and fuel. Printer : Ink :: Pencil : ? Graphite Writing/printing tool and material. Q. Common Analogy Traps \001 Near-synonyms vs exact synonyms: If the first pair is about synonym, the second pair should also be synonym, not a general association. \001 Part-whole confusion: Wheel:Car is not the same as Driver:Car. Driver is a person associated with the car, not a physical part. \001 Workplace confusion: Doctor:Hospital is profession:workplace. Doctor:Stethoscope is profession:tool. Identify which relation is present. \001 Cause-effect vs object-function: Rain:Flood is cause-effect; Knife:Cut is object-function. \001 Direction matters: Puppy:Dog is young:adult. Reversing it would be Dog:Puppy. Do not reverse the relationship. \001 Specificity matters: If a question says Artist:Painting, do not automatically choose a broad word like Art; look for the matching creator:creation relationship. \001 Use sentence testing: Convert A:B into a sentence such as 'A is related to B because ____'. Then apply exactly the same sentence frame to C:answer. R. 20 Rapid Analogy Drills Question Answer Relationship Bird : Nest :: Bee : ? Hive home/shelter Book : Read :: Food : ? Eat object and usual action Eye : See :: Ear : ? Hear organ and function Finger : Hand :: Leaf : ? Plant part-whole Teacher : Student :: Doctor : ? Patient professional and person served

Question Answer Relationship King : Palace :: Monk : ? Monastery person and residence Fish : Water :: Bird : ? Air natural environment Sugar : Sweet :: Lemon : ? Sour typical taste Day : Night :: Light : ? Darkness opposites Question : Answer :: Problem : ? Solution problem and resolution Seed : Plant :: Egg : ? Bird/Animal origin/development Army : Soldier :: Fleet : ? Ship group and member Hospital : Doctor :: School : ? Teacher institution and professional Book : Pages :: House : ? Rooms whole and internal units Clock : Time :: Thermometer : ? Temperature measuring instrument and quantity Poverty : Wealth :: Failure : ? Success opposites Begin : Commence :: Observe : ? Notice synonym Fear : Courage :: Weakness : ? Strength opposites Gold : Metal :: Rose : ? Flower class membership Driver : Vehicle :: Pilot : ? Aircraft person and operated vehicle 12. How She Should Study This Without Getting Overwhelmed Round 1 - Understand: Read the meaning and one example aloud. Round 2 - Recall: Cover the meaning and try to say it from the word/root. Round 3 - Contrast: For confused pairs and antonyms, say the difference in one sentence. Round 4 - Use: Make one fresh sentence of your own. Round 5 - Test: Only after the above, move to MCQs. Wrong answers become revision words. 5-minute daily vocabulary revision loop 1 minute: 10 old words -> 2 minutes: 5 confusing pairs -> 1 minute: 5 analogy relationships -> 1 minute: recall without looking. 13. Final Memory Checklist Area Remember this List of Words Meaning + synonym + antonym + context Confused Words Difference + one sentence for each word Phobias Root + thing feared Manias Root + obsession/preoccupation Prefixes Prefix meaning changes the base word Suffixes Suffix can change meaning or grammatical category Analogies Find exact relationship first Synonyms Choose closest contextual meaning Antonyms Check the exact opposite, not merely a different word One Word Substitution Learn the definition and the word together Idioms Use the contextual/figurative meaning, not literal meaning

Task 1 complete: Start with this learning pack and mark difficult words. No 100-question test is included in this task so that learning comes first. The next task can be prepared separately when you ask.
