pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS Vocabulary - Task 1 Very Easy Hinglish | Detailed Explanations | Maximum Useful Examples | Extended Analogies Purpose: Yeh task vocabulary ko pehle samajhne aur yaad rakhne ke liye hai. Abhi 100-question test nahi hai. Pehle concepts strong karenge, phir mixed Vocabulary + Grammar test, aur uske baad separate Vocabulary-only test karenge. Source note: Supplied syllabus image mein 10 vocabulary headings aur page ranges visible hain, lekin individual words visible nahi hain. Neeche ka content un headings ke basis par structured exam-prep learning material hai; ise supplied pages ka exact transcription nahi maana gaya hai. Golden rule: Word ko sirf Hindi meaning se mat ratna. Word -> easy meaning -> Hinglish -> example -> synonym/antonym -> recall. Isi sequence se padhna hai. 1. LIST OF WORDS - Sabse Pehle Basic Vocabulary 1. Abundant Meaning: more than enough Easy Hinglish: Bahut zyada; plenty. Sirf enough nahi, usually more than enough. Examples: The region has abundant rainfall. There was abundant food at the event. The garden has abundant flowers. The country has abundant sunlight. Exam Trap / Memory: Abundant = lots and lots. Opposite idea: scarce. 2. Adverse Meaning: unfavourable; harmful Easy Hinglish: Unfavourable ya negative situation. Examples: The match was cancelled due to adverse weather. Smoking can have adverse effects on health. The team worked under adverse conditions. The medicine caused an adverse reaction. Exam Trap / Memory: Adverse = situation favour mein nahi hai. 3. Alleviate Meaning: reduce pain or difficulty Easy Hinglish: Pain/problem ko kam karna. Examples: The medicine helped alleviate the pain. The new road may alleviate traffic. Rest can alleviate stress. The scheme aims to alleviate poverty. Exam Trap / Memory: Alleviate = reduce/relieve; problem ko completely khatam karna zaroori nahi. 4. Ambiguous Meaning: unclear; more than one possible meaning Easy Hinglish: Meaning clear nahi. Do interpretations possible ho sakte hain. Examples: His answer was ambiguous. The instructions were ambiguous. The sentence has an ambiguous meaning. Her ambiguous reply confused me. Exam Trap / Memory: Ambiguous = unclear or more than one possible meaning. 5. Benevolent Meaning: kind and generous Easy Hinglish: Dayalu, kind aur doosron ki help karne wala. Examples: The benevolent donor funded the library. The king was known for benevolent acts. She has a benevolent nature. A benevolent organisation helped the village.

Exam Trap / Memory: Benevolent = kind-hearted, not intelligent. 6. Candid Meaning: honest and direct Easy Hinglish: Seedha aur honest; gol-gol baat nahi. Examples: She gave a candid opinion. He was candid about his mistakes. Please be candid with me. The manager gave a candid reply. Exam Trap / Memory: Candid = frank/honest. 7. Coherent Meaning: logical and connected Easy Hinglish: Ideas aapas mein logically connected hon. Examples: Her explanation was coherent. The essay has a coherent structure. His argument was coherent. The paragraphs formed a coherent idea. Exam Trap / Memory: Coherent = ideas connected and sensible. 8. Conspicuous Meaning: easy to notice Easy Hinglish: Jo easily notice ho jaye. Examples: The bright red bag was conspicuous. His absence was conspicuous. The sign was conspicuous from a distance. She wore a conspicuous dress. Exam Trap / Memory: Conspicuous = noticeable; hidden iska opposite idea. 9. Diligent Meaning: hard-working and careful Easy Hinglish: Mehnati aur careful. Examples: She is a diligent student. A diligent worker checks details. He is diligent in his studies. Her diligent practice improved her score. Exam Trap / Memory: Diligent = steady, careful hard work. 10. Eloquent Meaning: fluent and persuasive Easy Hinglish: Achhe aur effective tareeke se bolna ya likhna. Examples: He gave an eloquent speech. She wrote an eloquent letter. The speaker was eloquent. His eloquent answer impressed the panel. Exam Trap / Memory: Eloquent ko speech/writing se connect karo. 11. Frugal Meaning: careful with money Easy Hinglish: Paise wisely spend karna; faltu kharcha nahi. Examples: He is frugal with money. A frugal person compares prices. They follow a frugal lifestyle. Frugal spending helped her save. Exam Trap / Memory: Frugal sensible spending hai; miserly bahut zyada spend na karne wala hota hai. 12. Imminent Meaning: about to happen

Easy Hinglish: Bahut jaldi hone wala. Examples: A storm is imminent. The launch is imminent. An announcement is imminent. The final exam is imminent. Exam Trap / Memory: Imminent = very near in time, not important. 13. Meticulous Meaning: very careful about details Easy Hinglish: Har chhoti detail ka bahut dhyan. Examples: She is meticulous about her notes. The engineer was meticulous in checking the design. He keeps meticulous records. Her meticulous work had very few errors. Exam Trap / Memory: Meticulous = detail ka extreme care. 14. Obsolete Meaning: no longer useful or in use Easy Hinglish: Purana/outdated jo practically use mein nahi raha. Examples: The machine is obsolete. The technology became obsolete. The old software is obsolete. The company replaced its obsolete system. Exam Trap / Memory: Obsolete sirf old nahi; outdated and no longer useful. 15. Pragmatic Meaning: practical and realistic Easy Hinglish: Reality ke according practical solution. Examples: We need a pragmatic solution. She took a pragmatic approach. His decision was pragmatic. The team adopted a pragmatic plan. Exam Trap / Memory: Pragmatic = practical, reality-based. 16. Reluctant Meaning: unwilling; hesitant Easy Hinglish: Mann nahi hai ya hesitation hai. Examples: He was reluctant to speak. She was reluctant to join. I was reluctant to change the plan. The child was reluctant to answer. Exam Trap / Memory: Reluctant = unwilling/hesitant; opposite idea eager/willing. 17. Scrutinise Meaning: examine very carefully Easy Hinglish: Bahut dhyan se detail mein check karna. Examples: Please scrutinise the report. The officer scrutinised the documents. The teacher scrutinised every answer. We should scrutinise the contract. Exam Trap / Memory: Scrutinise = deeply examine. 18. Vigilant Meaning: alert and watchful

Easy Hinglish: Chaukanna aur alert. Examples: Security guards remained vigilant. Stay vigilant online. The police were vigilant. A vigilant student notices small errors. Exam Trap / Memory: Vigilant = alert/watchful. 19. Viable Meaning: capable of working successfully Easy Hinglish: Jo realistically kaam kar sakta ho; workable. Examples: The project is financially viable. We need a viable solution. The plan is viable with a small budget. The business model is viable. Exam Trap / Memory: Viable = workable/feasible. 20. Wary Meaning: cautious because of possible danger Easy Hinglish: Danger ho sakta hai, isliye savdhaan. Examples: Be wary of unknown websites. She was wary of the stranger. He is wary of quick decisions. Consumers should be wary of fake offers. Exam Trap / Memory: Wary = cautious. Weary = tired. 21. Resilient Meaning: able to recover after difficulty Easy Hinglish: Problem/failure ke baad recover karna. Examples: She remained resilient after failure. The team was resilient after the loss. Children can be surprisingly resilient. The business proved resilient during difficulty. Exam Trap / Memory: Resilient = setback ke baad bounce back. 22. Lucid Meaning: clear and easy to understand Easy Hinglish: Clear aur easily samajh aane wala. Examples: Her explanation was lucid. The teacher gave a lucid example. The report is lucid. He gave a lucid answer. Exam Trap / Memory: Lucid explanation = confusion kam. 23. Vague Meaning: not clear or exact Easy Hinglish: Exact details clear nahi. Examples: His reply was vague. The instructions were vague. She gave a vague description. The plan is still vague. Exam Trap / Memory: Vague = details insufficient. Ambiguous = more than one possible meaning. 24. Hostile Meaning: unfriendly; aggressive Easy Hinglish: Unfriendly, opposing ya aggressive. Examples: The crowd became hostile. He received a hostile response. The environment was hostile. The two groups were openly hostile.

Exam Trap / Memory: Hostile ka opposite friendly/cooperative. 25. Impartial Meaning: unbiased; not taking sides Easy Hinglish: Kisi side favour na karna. Examples: A judge should be impartial. The referee remained impartial. We need an impartial investigation. She gave an impartial opinion. Exam Trap / Memory: Impartial = unbiased/neutral. Core Word Recall - One Line Word Easy Synonym Opposite / Contrast Recall Abundant Plentiful Scarce Bahut zyada Adverse Unfavourable Favourable Negative condition Alleviate Relieve Worsen Problem kam Ambiguous Unclear Clear Multiple possible meaning Benevolent Kind Cruel Dayalu Candid Frank Evasive Seedha honest Coherent Logical Incoherent Connected idea Conspicuous Noticeable Hidden Easy to notice Diligent Hard-working Negligent Careful mehnat Eloquent Expressive Inarticulate Powerful expression Frugal Economical Wasteful Smart spending Imminent Near Distant About to happen Meticulous Thorough Careless Detail-focused Obsolete Outdated Current Use se bahar Pragmatic Practical Impractical Reality-based Reluctant Unwilling Eager Mann nahi Scrutinise Examine closely Ignore Detail checking Vigilant Alert Careless Chaukanna Viable Workable Unworkable Actually workable Wary Cautious Reckless Danger se careful Resilient Able to recover Fragile Setback ke baad recover Lucid Clear Confusing Easy to understand Vague Unclear Specific Details missing Hostile Unfriendly Friendly Opposing Impartial Unbiased Biased No side 2. WORDS CONFUSED & MISUSED - Similar Dikhta Hai, Meaning Alag 1. Affect / Effect Meaning: Affect = usually verb, influence karna. Effect = usually noun, result.

Easy Hinglish: Action/influence -> affect; result -> effect. Examples: Stress can affect sleep. The effect of stress was obvious. Music affected my mood. The medicine had a positive effect. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 2. Accept / Except Meaning: Accept = receive/agree. Except = excluding. Easy Hinglish: Accept = lena/maan lena; except = chhodkar. Examples: I accept the offer. She accepted my apology. Everyone came except Riya. No one was absent except Aman. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 3. Advice / Advise Meaning: Advice = noun. Advise = verb. Easy Hinglish: Advice = salah; advise = salah dena. Examples: Her advice was useful. I need some advice. I advise you to revise. Doctors advise regular exercise. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 4. Principal / Principle Meaning: Principal = school head or main. Principle = rule/belief. Easy Hinglish: Principal = person/main; principle = rule. Examples: The principal addressed students. This is the principal reason. Honesty is a principle. He follows strong principles. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 5. Stationary / Stationery Meaning: Stationary = not moving. Stationery = writing materials. Easy Hinglish: Stationary = still; stationery = pens/paper. Examples: The bus remained stationary. The car was stationary. She bought stationery. The shop sells office stationery. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 6. Compliment / Complement Meaning: Compliment = praise. Complement = match/complete. Easy Hinglish: Compliment = tareef; complement = match/complete. Examples: She complimented my dress. He gave me a compliment. The shoes complement the dress. The sauce complements the meal. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 7. Loose / Lose Meaning: Loose = not tight. Lose = fail to keep/defeat.

Easy Hinglish: Loose = dhila; lose = khona/haar jana. Examples: This shirt is loose. The rope is loose. Do not lose your wallet. We may lose the match. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 8. Then / Than Meaning: Then = time/next step. Than = comparison. Easy Hinglish: Then = phir; than = comparison. Examples: Finish this, then rest. Then we went home. She is taller than me. This is better than that. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 9. Their / There / They're Meaning: Their = possession. There = place. They're = they are. Easy Hinglish: Their = unka; there = wahan; they're = they are. Examples: Their books are there. Put the bag there. They're ready. Their car is parked there. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 10. Your / You're Meaning: Your = possession. You're = you are. Easy Hinglish: Your = tumhara; you're = you are. Examples: Your answer is correct. Where is your bag? You're late. You're doing well. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 11. Its / It's Meaning: Its = possession. It's = it is/it has. Easy Hinglish: Its = iska; it's = it is/has. Examples: The dog wagged its tail. The company changed its logo. It's raining. It's been a long day. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 12. Desert / Dessert Meaning: Desert = dry region. Dessert = sweet dish. Easy Hinglish: Desert = registan; dessert = meetha. Examples: They crossed the desert. The desert is dry. We had dessert. Dessert was delicious. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 13. Elicit / Illicit Meaning: Elicit = draw out a response. Illicit = illegal.

Easy Hinglish: Elicit = response nikalna; illicit = illegal. Examples: The question elicited laughter. The interview elicited useful information. Illicit trade is banned. Police seized illicit goods. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 14. Farther / Further Meaning: Farther often physical distance. Further often additional/detail. Easy Hinglish: Farther = distance; further = extra/additional. Examples: The village is farther away. He ran farther than me. For further details, call us. We need further discussion. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 15. Fewer / Less Meaning: Fewer with countable nouns. Less with uncountable amount. Easy Hinglish: Fewer = countable; less = amount. Examples: Fewer students attended. There are fewer mistakes. Use less water. We need less sugar. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 16. Lie / Lay Meaning: Lie = recline. Lay = put something down. Easy Hinglish: Lie = khud letna; lay = object rakhna. Examples: I will lie down. He lies on the bed. Lay the book here. She laid the bag on the table. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 17. Wary / Weary Meaning: Wary = cautious. Weary = tired. Easy Hinglish: Wary = savdhaan; weary = thaka hua. Examples: Be wary of scams. She was wary of strangers. I felt weary after travel. He was weary after studying all day. Exam Trap / Memory: Sentence mein exact meaning aur grammar role check karo. 3. PHOBIAS - Root Se Yaad Karo Term Fear/Association Root Cue Examples Fast Clue Acrophobia heights Acro -> high He avoids high balconies. / Looking down from a tall building scares him. Height clue -> Acropho bia. Claustrophobia enclosed/tight spaces Closed/tight space She feels uncomfortable in a crowded lift. / He avoids tiny closed rooms. Lift/clos ed room clue.

Term Fear/Association Root Cue Examples Fast Clue Agoraphobia certain public/open situations where escape may feel difficult Public/open setting association He avoids some crowded public places. / The passage described fear linked to certain public situations. Do not reduce it to only 'fear of open spaces'. Arachnophobia spiders Arachno -> spider She is frightened by spiders. / Seeing a spider makes him panic. Spider clue. Hydrophobia water Hydro -> water He avoids swimming. / Water-related fear was mentioned. Hydro -> water. Xenophobia strangers/foreigners Xeno -> strange/foreign The passage discussed fear of outsiders. / The group showed hostility toward foreigners. Foreign/ stranger clue. Nyctophobia darkness/night Nycto -> night He is afraid of complete darkness. / She dislikes being alone at night. Night/da rkness clue. Glossophobia public speaking Speech/tongue association She fears speaking before a crowd. / He became very anxious before his presentation. Public s peaking clue. Zoophobia animals Zoo -> animals He fears certain animals. / The child is afraid of many animals. Animal clue. Thanatophobia death Thanato -> death The story described fear of death. / The character constantly worried about dying. Death clue. Astraphobia thunder/lightning Storm/lightning She fears thunder and lightning. / The storm made him extremely frightened. Thunder /lightnin g clue. Phobias - Fast Recall Sentences Acrophobia = heights. Remember: Acro -> high. Examples: He avoids high balconies. / Looking down from a tall building scares him. Claustrophobia = enclosed/tight spaces. Remember: Closed/tight space. Examples: She feels uncomfortable in a crowded lift. / He avoids tiny closed rooms. Agoraphobia = certain public/open situations where escape may feel difficult. Remember: Public/open setting association. Examples: He avoids some crowded public places. / The passage described fear linked to certain public situations. Arachnophobia = spiders. Remember: Arachno -> spider. Examples: She is frightened by spiders. / Seeing a spider makes him panic. Hydrophobia = water. Remember: Hydro -> water. Examples: He avoids swimming. / Water-related fear was mentioned. Xenophobia = strangers/foreigners. Remember: Xeno -> strange/foreign. Examples: The passage discussed fear of outsiders. / The group showed hostility toward foreigners. Nyctophobia = darkness/night. Remember: Nycto -> night. Examples: He is afraid of complete darkness. / She dislikes being alone at night. Glossophobia = public speaking. Remember: Speech/tongue association. Examples: She fears speaking before a crowd. / He became very anxious before his presentation. Zoophobia = animals. Remember: Zoo -> animals. Examples: He fears certain animals. / The child is afraid of many animals.

Thanatophobia = death. Remember: Thanato -> death. Examples: The story described fear of death. / The character constantly worried about dying. Astraphobia = thunder/lightning. Remember: Storm/lightning. Examples: She fears thunder and lightning. / The storm made him extremely frightened. 4. MANIAS - Root + Association Term Association Root Cue Examples Re cal l Bibliomania books Biblio -> books He has an excessive preoccupation with collecting books. / Her room is full of books she keeps collecting. Bo ok clu e -> bibl io. Kleptomania stealing Klepto -> stealing The term refers to a recurrent urge to steal objects. / The definition contains an urge to steal. Ste alin g cl ue -> kle pto . Megalomania power/grandeur Mega -> great/big The character showed an exaggerated sense of power and importance. / He behaved as though he were above everyone. Po wer /gr and eur clu e -> me ga. Dipsomania alcohol Dipso -> alcohol-related The term is associated with compulsive craving for alcohol. / The definition mentions excessive craving for alcohol. Alc oho l cl ue -> dip so. Pyromania fire-setting Pyro -> fire The term is associated with an unusual fascination/urge involving fire-setting. / The story focused on an urge related to fire. Fire clu e -> pyr o. Graphomania writing Grapho -> writing She had an excessive urge to write. / He kept writing constantly. Wri tin g cl ue -> gra pho .

Term Association Root Cue Examples Re cal l Erotomania erotic/love-related delusional preoccupation Eroto -> erotic/love The term describes an unusual fixed preoccupation involving being loved. / The definition gives a love-related delusional belief. Lov e/e roti c cl ue -> ero to. 5. PREFIXES & SUFFIXES - Unfamiliar Word Ko Todkar Samjho Prefix word ke beginning mein hota hai. Suffix word ke end mein. Base word pehle identify karo. Prefix Meaning Many Examples Break-down un- not/opposite unhappy, unfair, unknown, unable, unusual, unsafe un + happy -> not happy dis- not/opposite/separation disagree, dishonest, dislike, disconnect, disappear, distrust dis + agree -> not agree in- not inactive, incorrect, incomplete, invisible, indirect in + active -> not active im- not impossible, impatient, imperfect, immature, impolite im + possible -> not possible il- not illegal, illogical, illegible il + legal -> not legal ir- not irregular, irrelevant, irresponsible, irrational ir + regular -> not regular re- again/back rewrite, reread, rebuild, revisit, reconsider, restart re + write -> write again pre- before preview, prepay, pretest, prebook, prehistoric pre + view -> view before post- after postgraduate, postwar, posttest, postmodern post + test -> after test anti- against antiwar, antivirus, antisocial, anti-smoking anti -> against auto- self autobiography, automatic, autopilot, automobile auto -> self bi- two bilingual, bicycle, bilateral, biannual bi -> two tri- three triangle, tricycle, tripod, trilingual tri -> three mis- wrong/badly misunderstand, mislead, misuse, misplace, miscalculate mis -> wrongly co- together/with cooperate, coexist, coauthor, coworker, cofounder co -> together sub- under/below subway, submarine, substandard, subconscious sub -> under/below super- above/beyond superhuman, supermarket, superpower, supersede super -> above/beyond inter- between/among international, interact, interconnect, interschool inter -> between trans- across/beyond transport, transfer, transform, transnational trans -> across Suffix Function Many Examples Break-down -ness state/quality kindness, darkness, happiness, weakness, fairness, carefulness kind -> kindness -ment action/result development, movement, agreement, improvement, payment, achievement develop -> development

Suffix Function Many Examples Break-down -tion / -sion noun form creation, education, decision, expansion, revision, discussion decide -> decision -er / -or person who does teacher, writer, actor, inventor, conductor, creator teach -> teacher -ful full of helpful, useful, careful, hopeful, beautiful, successful help -> helpful -less without hopeless, careless, fearless, useless, endless, powerless hope -> hopeless -able / -ible capable of being readable, comfortable, visible, flexible, possible, reversible read -> readable -ous having a quality dangerous, famous, curious, nervous, generous, adventurous danger -> dangerous -ive having/relating to active, effective, creative, attractive, protective create -> creative -ly often forms adverbs quickly, slowly, carefully, clearly, happily, wisely quick -> quickly 6. SYNONYMS - Closest Meaning Practice Word Synonyms Examples Abandon leave / desert He abandoned the plan. / They left the village. Accurate correct / precise The answer is accurate. / The measurement is precise. Brief short / concise Give a brief answer. / Keep the response concise. Cautious careful / wary Be cautious online. / She was wary of scams. Commence begin / start The meeting commenced. / The meeting began. Conceal hide He concealed the truth. / She hid the letter. Conspicuous noticeable / obvious The stain was conspicuous. / The error was noticeable. Diminish reduce / decrease The noise diminished. / The pain decreased. Evident clear / obvious The mistake was evident. / The reason was obvious. Fragile delicate / breakable The glass is fragile. / The item is delicate. Generous giving She is generous with her time. Hostile unfriendly / antagonistic The crowd became hostile. Impartial unbiased / neutral The judge was impartial. Lucid clear / intelligible Her explanation was lucid. Meticulous thorough / careful He is meticulous about records. Obsolete outdated / outmoded The device is obsolete. Pragmatic practical / realistic We need a pragmatic approach. Reluctant unwilling / hesitant He was reluctant to answer. Resilient tough / able to recover The team remained resilient. Scrutinise examine closely / inspect Scrutinise the document. Vague unclear / indefinite His reply was vague. Vigilant alert / watchful Security stayed vigilant. Viable workable / feasible The plan is viable.

7. ANTONYMS - Exact Opposite Pakdo Word Antonym Example Pair Abundant Scarce abundant resources / scarce resources Ancient Modern ancient temple / modern building Artificial Natural artificial light / natural light Expand Contract business expands / market contracts Permanent Temporary permanent job / temporary arrangement Optimistic Pessimistic optimistic view / pessimistic view Generous Stingy generous person / stingy person Hostile Friendly hostile response / friendly response Victory Defeat victory / defeat Transparent Opaque transparent glass / opaque material Superior Inferior superior quality / inferior quality Maximum Minimum maximum value / minimum value Include Exclude include all / exclude one Encourage Discourage encourage effort / discourage effort Reveal Conceal reveal secret / conceal secret Create Destroy create a system / destroy a system Accept Reject accept offer / reject offer Flexible Rigid flexible rules / rigid rules Complex Simple complex problem / simple problem Frequent Rare frequent visits / rare visits Vivid Dull vivid memory / dull image Mandatory Optional mandatory training / optional training Reluctant Eager reluctant to go / eager to go Visible Hidden visible object / hidden object Genuine Fake genuine product / fake product 8. ONE WORD SUBSTITUTION - Definition -> Exact Word Definition Answer Memory Cue Example A person who loves books Bibliophile Biblio = books A bibliophile collects or loves books. A person who hates mankind Misanthrope Misanthro = dislike of people A misanthrope dislikes human society. A person who helps humanity through charity Philanthropist Philanthro = love of humanity The philanthropist donated to the school. A person who knows many languages Polyglot Poly = many She is a polyglot. Study of human beings Anthropology Anthropo = human Anthropology studies humans and cultures. Study of plants Botany plants Botany is the study of plants. Study of animals Zoology zoo = animals Zoology is the study of animals.

Definition Answer Memory Cue Example Unable to read or write Illiterate literacy absent The adult was illiterate. One who speaks very little Taciturn quiet/reserved He is taciturn in meetings. One who believes in God Theist theism A theist believes in God. One who does not believe in God Atheist a + theist An atheist does not believe in God. One who believes in one God Monotheist mono = one A monotheist believes in one God. One who believes in many gods Polytheist poly = many A polytheist believes in many gods. One who does not take sides Impartial unbiased An impartial judge avoids favouritism. Place where aircraft are kept Hangar aircraft storage The aircraft returned to the hangar. Place where dead bodies are kept Morgue morgue The body was taken to the morgue. Person who collects stamps Philatelist stamp collector The philatelist collects stamps. Person who collects coins Numismatist coin collector The numismatist studies old coins. Government by the people Democracy demo = people Democracy is government by the people. Government by a king or queen Monarchy monarch The kingdom was a monarchy. Person who writes dictionaries Lexicographer lexicon/dictionary The lexicographer compiled a dictionary. Person who writes own life story Autobiographer auto = self The author was an autobiographer. One who travels from place to place Itinerant travelling An itinerant worker moved between towns. A place where books are kept Library book collection Students studied in the library. A place where animals are kept/displayed Zoo animal collection The family visited the zoo. 9. IDIOMS / PHRASES - Literal Meaning Nahi Lena Idiom Meaning Example Easy Hinglish Break the ice start a friendly interaction A joke helped break the ice. New class/meeting mein awkwardness kam karna. Once in a blue moon very rarely He visits us once in a blue moon. Bahut rarely. A blessing in disguise bad-looking thing that later helps Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise. Pehle bura, baad mein useful. Hit the nail on the head say exactly the right thing You hit the nail on the head. Bilkul exact point pakadna. Spill the beans reveal a secret She spilled the beans. Secret bata dena. Beat around the bush avoid the main point Stop beating around the bush. Main point avoid karna. Cost an arm and a leg be very expensive That phone costs an arm and a leg. Bahut expensive. Under the weather feel unwell I am under the weather. Tabiyat kharab/low feel.

Idiom Meaning Example Easy Hinglish Call it a day stop work for the day Let's call it a day. Aaj ka work band. In hot water be in trouble He is in hot water. Problem mein hona. Piece of cake very easy The question was a piece of cake. Bahut easy. Burn the midnight oil work/study late She burned the midnight oil. Late night study/work. At the eleventh hour at the last moment He submitted it at the eleventh hour. Last moment par. A storm in a teacup big reaction to small issue Their argument was a storm in a teacup. Chhoti baat ka bada issue. By leaps and bounds very rapidly Her English improved by leaps and bounds. Bahut fast improvement. Keep an eye on watch carefully Keep an eye on the timer. Dhyan se dekhna. Make both ends meet manage expenses with income They work hard to make both ends meet. Income se expenses manage karna. On cloud nine extremely happy She was on cloud nine. Bahut zyada khush. Add fuel to the fire make a bad situation worse His comment added fuel to the fire. Situation aur kharab karna. Bite the bullet face difficulty bravely She bit the bullet and attempted the hard section. Mushkil cheez courage se face karna. Read between the lines understand hidden meaning Read between the lines. Hidden meaning samajhna. In the long run over a long period Revision helps in the long run. Long term mein. On the same page have same understanding We are on the same page. Same understanding. A double-edged sword both positive and negative Technology can be a double-edged sword. Benefit + harm dono. Tip of the iceberg small visible part of larger issue This error is only the tip of the iceberg. Visible part chhota, issue bada. Go the extra mile make extra effort She went the extra mile. Extra effort karna. Take with a grain of salt do not accept fully without checking Take that rumour with a grain of salt. Blindly true mat maano. Get cold feet become nervous and back out He got cold feet before the presentation. Last moment par darr jana. Pull strings use influence He pulled strings to arrange the meeting. Influence use karna. Turn a blind eye deliberately ignore The supervisor turned a blind eye. Jaan-bujhkar ignore. Cut corners skip proper steps Do not cut corners in preparation. Shortcut ke chakkar mein quality skip. Through thick and thin in good and bad times They stayed together through thick and thin. Achhe-bure dono time saath. In black and white in writing/clearly stated The rule is in black and white. Written/clear form. At loggerheads in strong disagreement The two groups are at loggerheads. Strongly disagree. In the nick of time just before too late She arrived in the nick of time. Bilkul last safe moment par. By word of mouth through people telling others The caf\001 became popular by word of mouth. Logon ke through spread. Keep at bay keep away/prevent harm Exercise helps keep stress at bay. Door/control mein rakhna. Put off postpone Do not put off revision. Delay karna.

contentSample: MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar + Figures of Speech + Vocabulary Master Guide A CET-oriented revision book for grammar, error spotting, sentence correction, vocabulary, RC support and common figures of speech. How this was built The uploaded MAH-MBA/MMS-CET 2026 sample material shows Verbal Ability/RC questions including error spotting and sentence-correc
pages: MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 1 MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar + Figures of Speech + Vocabulary Master Guide A CET-oriented revision book for grammar, error spotting, sentence correction, vocabulary, RC support and common figures of speech. How this was built The uploaded MAH-MBA/MMS-CET 2026 sample material shows Verbal Ability/RC questions including error spotting and sentence-correction formats. The expanded grammar and figure-of-speech sections below are supplementary preparation material so the learner has one complete revision book. 1. PARTS OF SPEECH Topic Meaning Example Exam focus Noun Name of a person, place, thing, animal, or idea. student, Mumbai, honesty Common types: proper, common, collective, abstract, material; countable/uncountable. Pronoun Replaces a noun. he, she, they, who, which, mine Watch person/case: I/me, he/him, who/whom; possessives: my/mine, their/theirs. Adjective Describes or qualifies a noun/pronoun. bright, five, beautiful Degrees: positive, comparative, superlative. Verb Shows an action, state, or occurrence. run, is, become Main/helping/modal verbs; transitive/intransitive; finite/non-finite. Adverb Modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. quickly, very, often Common groups: manner, place, time, frequency, degree. Preposition Shows relation of a noun/pronoun to another word. in, on, at, between, among Time/place and fixed combinations matter in questions. Conjunction Connects words, phrases, or clauses. and, but, because, although Coordinating, subordinating and correlative pairs. Interjection Expresses sudden feeling or reaction. oh!, wow!, alas! Usually stands apart from sentence structure. Article / Determiner Limits or identifies a noun. a, an, the, this, some, many Use a/an by sound, not spelling; the is used for specific/known items. 2. ARTICLES & DETERMINERS High-yield rules for a/an/the and common determiners. a - Before a consonant sound. Example: a book, a university, a European an - Before a vowel sound. Example: an apple, an hour, an MBA the - Specific, known, unique, or previously mentioned. Example: the sun, the book I bought no article - General plural/uncountable use in many contexts. Example: Books are useful. Milk is healthy. some/any - Quantity; some often in affirmative, any common in negatives/questions. Example: some water; any questions? many/much - many + countable; much + uncountable. Example: many books; much time

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 2 Trap Choose a/an by pronunciation: a university, an honest person, an MBA student. 3. NOUNS Forms, countability and common exam traps. Singular/plural: book/books; child/children; man/men; criterion/criteria (advanced). Countable: a book, two books. Uncountable: information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment. Possessive: Rahul's book; students' bags; children's toys. Collective nouns: team, committee, family, audience. The verb can depend on whether the group is treated as one unit or as individuals; in entrance tests, follow the sentence meaning. 4. PRONOUNS Case, agreement and relative pronouns. Subject: I, he, she, we, they. Object: me, him, her, us, them. Possessive: my/mine, your/yours, their/theirs. Who usually acts as the subject of a relative clause; whom is used for an object in formal usage. Which commonly refers to things; that can refer to people or things in defining clauses. Agreement: Each/every/either/neither generally takes a singular verb in standard test grammar. 5. ADJECTIVES & DEGREES OF COMPARISON Positive: tall Comparative: taller / more beautiful Superlative: tallest / most beautiful Common irregulars: good-better-best; bad-worse-worst; little-less-least; many/much-more-most. Do not double: more better, most best, more taller are incorrect in standard exam grammar. 6. VERBS & SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT Simple rule: singular subject -> singular verb; plural subject -> plural verb. He goes; they go. Words between subject and verb do not change agreement: The bouquet of roses is beautiful. Each/every/neither/either: usually singular in test-style agreement. Each student has a card. Either/or and neither/nor: the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject: Neither the manager nor the employees were ready. 7. TENSES Tense Use Example Simple Present habit/fact She studies every day. Present Continuous action happening now/around now She is studying now. Present Perfect past action with present relevance She has finished the test. Present Perfect Continuous action continuing up to now She has been studying for two hours. Simple Past completed past action She studied yesterday. Past Continuous action in progress in past She was studying at 6 pm.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 3 Tense Use Example Past Perfect earlier past before another past event She had left before I arrived. Past Perfect Continuous ongoing earlier-past duration She had been studying for two hours before dinner. Simple Future future action/prediction She will study tomorrow. Future Continuous ongoing future action She will be studying at 7 pm. Future Perfect completed before future point She will have finished by Monday. Future Perfect Continuous duration up to a future point She will have been studying for two hours by 8 pm. 8. ADVERBS Manner: carefully; place: here; time: yesterday; frequency: often; degree: very. Common trap: quick is an adjective, quickly is an adverb. She is a quick learner; she learns quickly. Position: frequency adverbs often come before the main verb (She often studies) but after forms of be (She is often late). 9. PREPOSITIONS Time: at 5 pm, on Monday, in July. Place: at the station, on the table, in the room. Common pairs: interested in, good at, afraid of, depend on, capable of, responsible for, different from. Between is commonly used for two; among for more than two in standard teaching grammar. 10. CONJUNCTIONS Coordinating: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so (FANBOYS). Subordinating: because, although, while, if, unless, since, before, after, whereas. Correlative: either...or, neither...nor, both...and, not only...but also. 11. PHRASES & CLAUSES Phrase: a group of words without a finite verb acting as a unit: in the morning, very quickly. Independent clause: can stand alone. Dependent clause: cannot stand alone and begins with a subordinator/relative marker in many cases. Noun clause: I know what she wants . Adjective/relative clause: the book that I bought . Adverb clause: I left because it was late . 12. GERUNDS, INFINITIVES & PARTICIPLES Gerund (-ing): functions as a noun - Swimming is healthy. Infinitive: to + base verb - I want to study. Participle: verb form acting adjectivally or in verb phrases - a broken chair; a smiling child; she is studying. Modifier trap The opening modifier should logically describe the subject: Walking down the road, I saw a dog. Avoid dangling forms such as Walking down the road, the rain started. 13. MODALS can/could: ability, possibility, polite request.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 4 may/might: possibility, permission. must: necessity/strong obligation. should/ought to: advice/duty. will/would: future, willingness, polite request, conditional sense. shall: formal suggestion/offer in some contexts. 14. ACTIVE & PASSIVE VOICE Active: The committee approved the plan. Passive: The plan was approved by the committee. Core pattern: object + appropriate form of be + past participle (+ by + agent when needed). Preserve tense. 15. DIRECT & INDIRECT SPEECH Direct: She said, "I am tired." Indirect: She said that she was tired. Watch pronouns, tense backshift where appropriate, time/place words (today -> that day, tomorrow -> the next day, here -> there), and question structure. 16. CONDITIONALS Type Meaning Example Zero general truth If you heat ice, it melts. First real/possible future If she studies, she will improve. Second unreal/hypothetical present/future If she studied more, she would improve. Third unreal past If she had studied, she would have improved. 17. QUESTION TAGS Positive statement -> negative tag: She is ready, isn't she? Negative statement -> positive tag: She isn't ready, is she? The auxiliary in the statement usually returns in the tag; match the subject pronoun. 18. COMMON ERROR-SPOTTING AREAS \177 Subject-verb agreement: Each student has a card. \177 Article use: He is an honest person. \177 Pronoun case: Riya and I went there; the teacher called Riya and me . \177 Tense consistency: She completed the work yesterday. \177 Prepositions: interested in , depend on . \177 Comparison: more useful, not more better. \177 Word form: She answered quickly , not quick. \177 Parallelism: She likes reading, writing and speaking . \177 Modifiers: make sure the opening phrase clearly describes the subject.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 5 19. FIGURES OF SPEECH - COMPLETE QUICK GUIDE These are supplementary language concepts. They are useful for English awareness, vocabulary and interpretation even though the uploaded CET sample specifically demonstrates other verbal formats. Figure Meaning Example Simile Direct comparison using like/as. Her smile was like sunshine. Metaphor Implied comparison without like/as. Time is a thief. Personification Giving human qualities to non-human things. The wind whispered. Hyperbole Deliberate exaggeration. I have told you a million times. Alliteration Repetition of initial consonant sounds. Wild winds whistle. Onomatopoeia Word imitates a sound. buzz, splash, clang Oxymoron Two apparently contradictory words placed together. deafening silence Pun Wordplay based on multiple meanings/similar sounds. A bicycle can't stand alone because it is two-tired. Irony Meaning/result contrasts with expectation or literal wording. A fire station burns down. Apostrophe Directly addressing an absent person, abstract idea or object. O Death, where is thy sting? Metonymy Related term substitutes for the thing/person. The crown announced... Synecdoche Part represents whole or whole represents part. All hands on deck. Euphemism Mild expression replacing a blunt one. passed away Antithesis Contrasting ideas placed in balanced form. Speech is silver; silence is golden. Anaphora Repetition at the beginning of successive clauses. We will learn. We will grow. We will succeed. Repetition Repeated word/phrase for emphasis. Never, never give up. Assonance Repetition of vowel sounds. The mellow wedding bells. Consonance Repetition of consonant sounds, not necessarily at the beginning. The lumpy, bumpy road. Allusion Brief reference to a known person, event, text or idea. He met his Waterloo. Paradox Apparently contradictory statement that may reveal a truth. Less is more. Litotes Understatement using a negative to express a positive/affirmation. Not a bad idea. Climax Ideas rise in order of importance or intensity. He whispered, spoke, shouted. Anticlimax A sudden drop from serious/high to ordinary or trivial. He lost his job, his house, and his pen. Chiasmus Reversal of grammatical structure in a parallel phrase. Ask not what your country can do for you... Transferred Epithet An adjective is transferred from the person/thing it logically describes to another noun. a sleepless night Zeugma One word governs two others in different senses. She broke his car and his heart. 20. VOCABULARY & VERBAL SKILLS

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 6 Skill Definition Example Synonym word with similar meaning rapid - quick Antonym word with opposite meaning ancient - modern Homophone same sound, different spelling/meaning their/there Homonym same spelling/sound with different meanings depending on use bank One-word substitution single word replacing a phrase one who loves books - bibliophile Idiom fixed expression whose meaning is not literal break the ice Phrasal verb verb + particle with a distinct meaning give up, look after Collocation words that commonly occur together make a decision 21. SENTENCE CORRECTION CHECKLIST 1. Find the subject and main verb first. 2. Check singular/plural agreement. 3. Check tense and time expression. 4. Check pronoun case and antecedent. 5. Check articles and determiners. 6. Check preposition/collocation. 7. Check adjective vs adverb. 8. Check comparison forms. 9. Check parallel structure. 10. Check modifier attachment. 11. Read the whole sentence for meaning. 22. MHT-CET-STYLE ATTACK METHOD Error spotting: read once for meaning, then scan subject-verb, tense, pronoun, article, preposition and word form. Sentence correction: eliminate choices that create agreement/tense/idiom errors; then choose the cleanest standard sentence. Fill in the blank: read the sentence before looking at options; identify the required part of speech and meaning. Vocabulary/RC: use context, not just memorised definitions. Revision rule Your friend has already completed Articles, Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives. Use the Mock 1 result to decide whether to revise these or move forward to verbs, adverbs, tenses, prepositions and sentence correction.

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET \001 Full VARC / English Mock 1 Page 2 PART 1 \001 READING COMPREHENSION: PASSAGE 1 Modern organisations increasingly rely on indicators to judge performance. Numbers such as tasks completed, calls answered, or items delivered are convenient because they can be compared across teams. Yet a measure is only a model of reality, not reality itself. A department may complete many tasks while producing errors that another department must repair. A support team may answer customers quickly without solving their actual problems. When the measured indicator becomes the only target, people may focus on improving the number rather than the underlying service. This does not mean that measurement should be abandoned. Instead, sensible evaluation combines quantitative indicators with quality checks, long-term outcomes, and evidence about unintended effects. A good metric starts a discussion about performance; it should not end that discussion. 1. What is the central idea of the passage? A. All performance measurement should stop. B. Metrics are useful but should not be treated as a complete picture of performance. C. Customer support should prioritise speed above all else. D. Numbers are always misleading. E. Only long-term outcomes matter. 2. The example of the support team shows that: A. speed guarantees satisfaction B. answering quickly does not necessarily resolve the underlying problem C. customers dislike phone support D. quality cannot be measured E. all calls should be longer 3. According to the passage, what may happen when a measure becomes the only target? A. People may prioritise the number over the real objective. B. People stop collecting data. C. Teams always become more accurate. D. Long-term outcomes improve automatically. E. Indicators become impossible to compare. 4. The phrase \003a model of reality\004 suggests that a metric: A. contains every possible detail B. is a simplified representation of something more complex C. is always false D. cannot be compared E. is useful only in science 5. The author\005s tone is best described as: A. hostile B. balanced and cautionary C. sarcastic D. celebratory E. indifferent 6. Which action would the author most likely recommend? A. Reward only the number of tasks completed. B. Ignore all numerical data. C. Combine metrics with quality checks and long-term outcomes. D. Use a single metric for every department. E. Evaluate performance only through opinions. 7. Which statement is NOT supported by the passage? A. Metrics can help compare teams. B. Errors can be created despite high task completion. C. Measurement should always be abandoned. D. A good metric can begin a performance discussion. E. A quick answer may fail to solve a problem. 8. \003Unintended effects\004 most nearly means: A. effects that were not planned or expected B. effects that were carefully designed

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET \001 Full VARC / English Mock 1 Page 3 C. effects that are impossible D. effects that are always positive E. effects that have no cause 9. What can be inferred from the passage? A. The same metric may not fully describe every type of work. B. Metrics are useless in every organisation. C. All teams should have identical goals. D. Quality is always easy to count. E. Only customer service needs evaluation. 10. Choose the best title. A. Why Organisations Should Avoid Data B. When Metrics Do Not Tell the Whole Story C. The End of Customer Service D. How to Complete More Tasks E. Numbers Without Meaning PART 2 \001 READING COMPREHENSION: PASSAGE 2 Urban green spaces are often defended because they make neighbourhoods more attractive. Their value, however, is not merely visual. Trees can provide shade, reduce heat around streets, and create habitats for birds and insects. Parks can also offer places for exercise and informal social contact. These benefits do not appear automatically whenever greenery is added. A park that is difficult to reach may remain underused, while trees planted without enough soil or maintenance may fail to thrive. Local conditions therefore matter: planners must consider access, safety, water, species selection, and the needs of nearby residents. Counting the number of trees or parks is convenient, but the more useful question is whether green spaces are healthy, accessible, and actually serving the community. 11. The main purpose of the passage is to: A. argue that parks are mainly decorative B. explain why the value of green spaces depends on planning and practical use C. claim that every neighbourhood needs the same number of trees D. show that urban wildlife is harmful E. compare cities with villages 12. Which benefit is NOT mentioned? A. shade B. habitats for wildlife C. opportunities for exercise D. informal social contact E. lower housing taxes 13. Why might a park remain underused? A. It contains too many trees. B. It is difficult to reach. C. It offers space for exercise. D. It has local residents nearby. E. It supports social contact. 14. The author suggests that counting trees is: A. completely useless B. sufficient to evaluate green spaces C. convenient but not enough by itself D. more important than maintenance E. the only way to measure public value 15. The tone of the passage is: A. practical and analytical B. angry C. humorous D. dismissive of parks

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET \001 Full VARC / English Mock 1 Page 4 E. overly emotional 16. The phrase \003These benefits do not appear automatically\004 means: A. green spaces never help B. benefits depend on conditions and implementation C. trees are always harmful D. parks must be privately owned E. access is irrelevant 17. Tree numbers alone reveal community benefit. D. Maintenance is optional. E. Urban green spaces have no social role. 19. MAH-MBA/MMS-CET | Full VARC / English Syllabus Mock Page 2 Reading Comprehension - Passage 1 Organisations often adopt digital tools expecting immediate productivity gains. Yet a tool's impact depends less on its features than on how work is organised around it. When a team digitises a confusing process without reconsidering the process itself, the confusion may simply move onto a screen. Conversely, a modest tool can be valuable if responsibilities are clear, staff are trained, and feedback is used to improve the workflow. Technology can reduce repetitive effort, but it does not automatically settle questions about priorities or accountability. A successful implementation therefore treats software as part of a wider system of people, routines, and decisions. Before asking which tool is most powerful, organisations should ask what problem they are trying to solve and how they will know whether it has been solved. 1. What is the central idea of the passage? A. Organisations should replace all manual work with digital tools. B. Digital tools improve productivity only when integrated with clear processes and goals. C. The most expensive software is usually the most effective. D. Staff training is unnecessary when software is powerful. E. Technology always creates accountability problems. 2. The statement that confusion may 'move onto a screen' means that: A. digital screens cause every workplace problem. B. software automatically makes a process simpler. C. digitising a poorly designed process does not fix the underlying problem. D. employees should avoid using screens. E. confusing processes cannot be improved. 3. Which factor is specifically mentioned as making a modest tool valuable? A. A large advertising budget B. Clear responsibilities and staff training C. A complicated interface D. Removing all feedback E. Using the newest technology 4. Which action should an organisation take before choosing a tool, according to the passage? A. Select the tool with the most features. B. Remove all existing routines. C. Identify the problem and define how success will be measured. D. Avoid consulting its staff. E. Digitise every process immediately. 6. Choose the most suitable title. A. Why Digital Tools Always Fail B. Technology Is Only Part of the System C. The End of Workplace Training D. How to Buy Expensive Software E. Why Feedback Slows Work

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET | Full VARC / English Syllabus Mock Page 3 Reading Comprehension - Passage 2 Public debates often reward confident statements more than careful qualifications. A speaker who says a policy will solve a problem may sound more persuasive than one who explains that the outcome depends on implementation, funding, and local conditions. However, confidence is not the same as evidence. Qualified language can reflect intellectual honesty rather than weakness, particularly when a problem has several causes. This does not mean that every claim should be treated as uncertain or that decision-makers should avoid action. It means that the strength of a conclusion should match the strength of the available evidence. Good judgement often requires both a willingness to act and a willingness to revise a decision when new information appears. 7. What is the main argument of the passage? A. Confident speakers are always correct. B. Decision-makers should postpone every decision. C. The certainty of a conclusion should be proportionate to the available evidence. D. Public debates should exclude policy discussions. E. Qualified language is a sign of poor leadership. 8. Why can qualified language be valuable? A. It can show intellectual honesty when a problem has several causes. B. It guarantees that a policy will work. C. It avoids the need for evidence. D. It prevents all disagreement. E. It makes decisions unnecessary. 9. Which statement is NOT supported by the passage? A. Confidence and evidence are different things. B. Decision-makers may need to revise decisions when new information appears. C. Every claim should be treated as uncertain and action should always be avoided. D. A problem may have several causes. E. A conclusion should reflect the available evidence. 10. B. the level of certainty should be justified by the quality of evidence. C. evidence matters only in scientific research. D. weak evidence always proves a claim false. E. all conclusions should remain equally uncertain. 11. Explanations are in Hinglish for quick learning and revision. 1. B - Digital tools improve productivity only when integrated with clear processes and goals. Hinglish explanation: Passage ka main idea hai ki technology akeli enough nahi; process, trained staff, responsibilities aur clear goal bhi zaroori hain. 2. C - digitising a poorly designed process does not fix the underlying problem. Hinglish explanation: Agar old process hi confusing hai, use screen par shift karne se core problem solve nahi hoti. Sirf format digital ho jata hai. 3. B - Clear responsibilities and staff training Hinglish explanation: Passage mein clear responsibilities, training aur feedback ko value create karne wale factors bataya gaya hai. 4. C - balanced and practical Hinglish explanation: Author technology ko na completely reject karta hai na blindly praise. Benefits ke saath limitations batata hai, isliye balanced/practical tone hai. 5. C - Identify the problem and define how success will be measured. Hinglish explanation: Last sentence clearly kehta hai pehle problem identify karo aur decide karo ki solution successful kaise measure hoga. 6. B - Technology Is Only Part of the System Hinglish explanation: Title poore passage ko capture karta hai: software ko people, routines aur decisions ke wider system mein dekhna chahiye. 7. C - The certainty of a conclusion should be proportionate to the available evidence. Hinglish explanation: Central message: claim ki certainty evidence ki strength ke proportion mein honi chahiye. 8. A - It can show intellectual honesty when a problem has several causes. Hinglish explanation: Complex issue mein qualification weakness nahi; uncertainty ko honestly acknowledge karna ho sakta hai. 9. C - Every claim should be treated as uncertain and action should always be avoided. Hinglish explanation: Passage explicitly kehta hai ki iska matlab yeh nahi ki action avoid karna chahiye ya har claim uncertain maana jaye. 10. B - the level of certainty should be justified by the quality of evidence. Hinglish explanation: Evidence jitna strong hai, conclusion ki certainty utni hi justified honi chahiye. Weak evidence se overconfident claim nahi karna. 11. A - measured and analytical Hinglish explanation: Author reasoned, measured language use karta hai aur dono extremes ko avoid karta hai. 12. A - is suitable Hinglish explanation: Formal standard agreement mein neither of + plural noun ko singular verb ke saath use kiya jata hai: neither ... is. 13. B - He completed the assignment yesterday. Hinglish explanation: Specific finished past time 'yesterday' ke saath simple past 'completed' use hota hai. 14. A - submit the report Hinglish explanation: Request/suggest/insist ke baad formal subjunctive structure mein base verb aata hai: requested that every employee submit. 15. A - than Hinglish explanation: Fixed pair 'No sooner ... than' hai. 16. A - of handling Hinglish explanation: Correct construction 'capable of + gerund/noun' hai: capable of handling. 17. B - The number of applicants has increased sharply. Hinglish explanation: 'The number of' ko singular noun phrase treat kiya jata hai: the number ... has increased. 18. A - Despite the heavy rain Hinglish explanation: 'Despite' ke baad directly noun phrase aata hai. 'In spite of' alag correct structure hai.

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET | Full VARC / English Syllabus Mock Page 12 19. A - to expand its services, improve customer support, and reduce costs Hinglish explanation: Parallelism mein list ke items same grammatical pattern follow karte hain: to expand, improve, reduce. 20. B - have received Hinglish explanation: 'Each' singular hai, isliye 'has received' hona chahiye. 21. B - for 2021 Hinglish explanation: Starting point year ke saath 'since 2021' use hota hai; 'for' duration ke saath. 22. C - are made Hinglish explanation: Furniture uncountable singular noun hai. Correct phrase 'is made' hoga. 23. D - all the evidences Hinglish explanation: Evidence aam taur par uncountable noun hai; standard usage 'all the evidence' hai. 24. E - No error Hinglish explanation: Sentence grammatically correct hai. Passive construction aur adverb placement dono acceptable hain. 25. B - who has represented Hinglish explanation: Relative clause mein 'who' plural 'performers' ko refer karta hai; 'who have represented' expected hai. 26. A - create Hinglish explanation: Speakers audience ko ignore karte hain to woh unintentionally confusion create kar sakte hain. 27. A - sequence Hinglish explanation: Supporting details ko logical sequence/order mein organise kiya jata hai. 28. A - received Hinglish explanation: Message intended way mein 'received' ya understood hua ya nahi, feedback batata hai. 29. A - opportunity Hinglish explanation: Respectful disagreement assumptions test karne ka opportunity ho sakta hai. 30. A - durable Hinglish explanation: Practical and durable solution sensible collocation hai: useful aur long-lasting solution. 31. A - alone Hinglish explanation: Sentence ka idea hai communication improve karne ke liye conscious practice chahiye; sirf repeatedly bolna alone enough nahi. 32. B - lessen Hinglish explanation: Mitigate ka meaning hota hai severity ya impact ko kam karna; closest synonym 'lessen' hai. 33. C - eager Hinglish explanation: Reluctant = unwilling/hesitant. Iska opposite eager ya willing hai. 34. B - ornithologist Hinglish explanation: Ornithologist birds ka study karta hai. Entomologist insects, archaeologist past human societies/artifacts, geologist Earth ka study karta hai. 35. B - to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem Hinglish explanation: Idiom ka matlab hai bilkul sahi point identify karna ya exact baat kehna. 36. B - Accommodation Hinglish explanation: Correct spelling accommodation hai; double c aur double m yaad rakho. 37. B - The weather can affect the delivery schedule. Hinglish explanation: Affect usually verb hai meaning influence. Effect usually noun hai meaning result. 'Weather can affect...' is correct. 38. A - S-Q-P-R Hinglish explanation: S overall goal introduce karta hai, Q evidence batata hai, P action/result, aur R change ke baad outcome deta hai. Order S-Q-P-R.

MAH-MBA/MMS-CET | Full VARC / English Syllabus Mock Page 13 39. A - Q-S-P-R Hinglish explanation: Research sequence: question define (Q), data collect (S), results compare (P), findings interpret (R). 40. A - Q-R-S-P Hinglish explanation: Complaint (Q) ke baad team review (R), unnecessary approvals remove (S), phir wait time reduce hota hai (P). 41. A - R-S-P-Q Hinglish explanation: R problem introduce karta hai, S initial explanation, P us explanation ke against evidence, Q next investigation. Order R-S-P-Q. 42. B - A new software system was introduced at the same time and automated several routine tasks. Hinglish explanation: New software ek alternative cause hai jo productivity rise explain kar sakta hai; training hi cause thi, is claim ko weaken karta hai. 43. B - Poor visibility contributes to at least some nighttime accidents. Hinglish explanation: Argument ka core link visibility aur accidents ke beech hai. Poor visibility kuch accidents ka factor hona chahiye, tab streetlights se reduction plausible hai. 44. C - Frequent customers are more likely to sign up for the card in the first place. Hinglish explanation: Selection/reverse causation possible hai: high-spending customers card lete hon, card ki wajah se spend badha ho zaroori nahi. 45. B - Application X will be reviewed. Hinglish explanation: Given rule directly kehta hai ki before-deadline received applications review hoti hain. X ne condition meet ki, so it will be reviewed. 46. B - Many customers began ordering through its online store, which remained available all day. Hinglish explanation: Online store reduced physical opening hours ke bawajood sales increase explain kar sakta hai. Dono facts ek saath true ho sakte hain. 47. B - with Hinglish explanation: Correct phrase 'consistent with' hai. 48. A - therefore Hinglish explanation: Evidence limited hone ka result caution hai, isliye 'therefore' logical result connector hai. 49. B - make Hinglish explanation: Natural collocation 'make a decision' hai. 50. B - economical Hinglish explanation: Long-term cost ki baat ho rahi hai; economical option overall cost-effective hota hai.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 3 MOCK 1 - EXPLANATIONS 1. Choose the correct sentence. A) She is an honest girl. B) She is a honest girl. C) She is the honest girl. D) She is honest a girl. E) She is an honesty girl. Answer: A - "honest" begins with a vowel sound, so use an . 2. Choose the correct article. He is ___ European businessman. A) a B) an C) the D) no article E) one Answer: A - "European" starts with a /y/ sound, so use a . 3. Identify the incorrect part. Each of the students / have submitted / their assignment / on time. A) Each of the students B) have submitted C) their assignment D) on time E) No error Answer: B - Each is singular: has submitted . 4. Choose the correct pronoun. Riya and ___ went to the library. A) me B) myself C) I D) mine E) my Answer: C - The subject is compound and first-person: Riya and I . 5. Choose the correct sentence. A) This book is her's. B) This book is hers. C) This book is her. D) This book is she. E) This book is herself. Answer: B - Hers is the possessive pronoun; do not add an apostrophe. 6. The teacher asked Rahul and ___ to stay back. A) I B) myself C) mine D) me E) my Answer: D - The object form after "asked" is me . 7. Identify the error. Neither of the two boys / have completed / his homework / yet. A) Neither of the two boys B) have completed C) his homework D) yet E) No error Answer: B - Neither is singular here: has completed . 8. Choose the correct adjective. The movie was extremely ___. A) bored B) boring C) bore D) boredom E) boringly Answer: B - The movie causes boredom, so it is boring . 9. This is the ___ building in the area. A) tall B) taller C) tallest D) most tall E) more taller Answer: C - The superlative form is tallest . 10. Choose the correct sentence. A) She is more intelligent than her sister. B) She is most intelligent than her sister. C) She is more intelligent then her sister. D) She is intelligent more than her sister. E) She is the more intelligent than her sister. Answer: A - The correct comparison is more intelligent than . 11. She ___ to college every day. A) go B) going C) gone D) goes E) is go Answer: D - With she, simple present takes goes .

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 4 12. Identify the error. He don't / know / the answer / to this question. A) He don't B) know C) the answer D) to this question E) No error Answer: A - Use doesn't with he. 13. By the time we reached the station, the train ___. A) leaves B) left C) had left D) has left E) leaving Answer: C - The earlier past action is past perfect: had left . 14. Choose the correct sentence. A) She has completed her work yesterday. B) She completed her work yesterday. C) She had complete her work yesterday. D) She completing her work yesterday. E) She has complete her work yesterday. Answer: B - "Yesterday" takes simple past: completed . 15. If she ___ harder, she would have passed the examination. A) studies B) studied C) had studied D) has studied E) studying Answer: C - Third conditional: had studied ... would have passed. 16. Identify the error. The students was / waiting outside / the examination hall / for an hour. A) The students was B) waiting outside C) the examination hall D) for an hour E) No error Answer: A - Plural subject students -> were . 17. Neither the manager nor the employees ___ willing to accept the proposal. A) was B) is C) has D) were E) be Answer: D - With neither...nor, the nearer plural subject employees takes were . 18. She speaks English very ___. A) fluent B) fluently C) fluency D) more fluent E) fluentness Answer: B - Modify the verb speaks with the adverb fluently . 19. Choose the correct sentence. A) He drives careless. B) He drives carelessly. C) He careless drives. D) He driving careless. E) He is drive carelessly. Answer: B - The adverb modifying drives is carelessly . 20. Identify the error. She completed the assignment / quick / and submitted it / to the teacher. A) She completed the assignment B) quick C) and submitted it D) to the teacher E) No error Answer: B - The verb completed needs an adverb: quickly . 21. Choose the best correction: "One of my friend is preparing for the examination." A) One of my friends is preparing for the examination. B) One of my friend are preparing for the examination. C) One of my friends are preparing for the examination. D) One of my friend is prepare for the examination. E) No change required. Answer: A - One of + plural noun: one of my friends is . 22. Choose the correct sentence. A) The girl which won the prize is my friend. B) The girl who won the prize is my friend. C) The girl whom won the prize is my friend. D) The girl whose won the prize is my friend. E) The girl what won the prize is my friend. Answer: B - For a person as the subject of the relative clause, who is correct.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Preparation Page 5 23. Find the error. Every student in the class / were given / an opportunity / to participate. A) Every student in the class B) were given C) an opportunity D) to participate E) No error Answer: B - Every student is singular: was given . 24. Choose the best correction: "He is one of the best player in the team." A) He is one of the best players in the team. B) He is one of the better player in the team. C) He is one of the best player of the team. D) He is one of the most best players in the team. E) No change required. Answer: A - One of the + plural noun: best players . 25. Choose the correct sentence. A) Despite of being tired, she continued studying. B) Despite being tired, she continued studying. C) Despite she was tired, she continued studying. D) Despite of tired, she continued study. E) Despite being tiring, she continued studied. Answer: B - The correct construction is despite being tired . Score interpretation 0-10: rebuild basics; 11-16: foundation is forming; 17-21: good base, focus on speed and accuracy; 22-25: move into wider grammar and mixed verbal practice while still revising errors.

Q1: B Q2: B Q3: B Q4: D Q5: C Q6: B Q7: C Q8: C Q9: B Q10: B Q11: C Q12: B Q13: B Q14: C Q15: C Q16: D Q17: D Q18: C Q19: B Q20: A Q21: C Q22: B Q23: B Q24: D Q25: C Q26: B Q27: C Q28: C Q29: B Q30: B Q31: B Q32: B Q33: C Q34: A Q35: B Q36: B Q37: A Q38: A Q39: B Q40: B Q41: A Q42: A Q43: B Q44: B Q45: B Q46: B Q47: C Q48: B Q49: A Q50: B QUICK EXPLANATIONS ARTICLES, DETERMINERS & NOUNS Q1 - B. \002Unusual\003 begins with a vowel sound, so \002an\003 is used. Q2 - B. \002University\003 begins with a /yu/ sound, so \002a\003 is used. Q3 - B. \002Students\003 is countable plural, so \002many more\003 fits. Q4 - D. \002Information\003 is uncountable; \002a little\003 means some amount. Q5 - C. The plural of \002criterion\003 is \002criteria\003. PRONOUNS, ADJECTIVES & COMPARISON Q6 - B. After the preposition \002to\003, the object form \002me\003 is required. Q7 - C. \002Whose\003 shows possession: the candidate\004s application. Q8 - C. An adjective is needed after \002were\003: \002clear\003. Q9 - B. For three or more items, the superlative form is used. Q10 - B. The standard construction is \002superior to\003. ADVERBS, VERBS & TENSES Q11 - C. The verb \002answered\003 is modified by the adverb \002confidently\003. Q12 - B. Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb. Q13 - B. The arrival happened before another past event, so past perfect is used. Q14 - C. An ongoing action before another past event uses past perfect continuous. Q15 - C. \002So far\003 commonly signals present perfect for an experience continuing to the present. SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT, PREPOSITIONS & CONJUNCTIONS Q16 - D. With \002neither...nor\003, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, \002players\003. Q17 - D. The head noun is singular: \002pair\003 -> \002is\003. Q18 - C. The fixed expression is \002interested in\003. Q19 - B. \002Divided into\003 is the standard expression. Q20 - A. \002Or\003 connects alternatives.

MHT-CET MBA/MMS English Grammar Mock 3 - Fresh Question Set Page 12 Q21 - C. The correct pair is \002neither...nor\003. MODALS, CONDITIONALS, VOICE & NARRATION Q22 - B. \002Should\003 expresses advice or recommendation. Q23 - B. \002May I...?\003 is a standard polite request for permission. Q24 - D. Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Q25 - C. Future passive uses \002will be + past participle\003. Q26 - B. Backshift changes present perfect to past perfect, and pronouns change. GERUNDS, INFINITIVES, PARTICIPLES & PARALLELISM Q27 - C. After the preposition \002in\003, a gerund (-ing form) is used. Q28 - C. \002Decide\003 is followed by a to-infinitive. Q29 - B. \002Fallen\003 acts as an adjective describing the leaves. Q30 - B. The three items should use the same -ing form. Q31 - B. \002Let us\003 for a suggestion takes the tag \002shall we?\003. CLAUSES, CONFUSING WORDS & SENTENCE CORRECTION Q32 - B. \002When\003 is used for the time of arrival. Q33 - C. \002Whom\003 can function as the object of \002hired\003. Q34 - A. \002Affect\003 is the verb meaning influence. Q35 - B. \002Accept\003 means receive or agree to. Q36 - B. The standard pattern is \002capable of + gerund\003. Q37 - A. \002Accustomed to\003 is followed by a noun or gerund; \002waking\003 is correct here. Q38 - A. \002Furniture\003 is an uncountable singular noun. ERROR SPOTTING - CET STYLE Q39 - B. \002Neither\003 is singular here, so \002was accepted\003 is required. Q40 - B. The head noun \002quality\003 is singular: \002has improved\003. Q41 - A. A finished past time marker like \002yesterday\003 normally takes simple past: \002discussed\003. Q42 - A. After \002one of my\003, use a plural noun: \002friends\003. Q43 - B. Use \002explained the concept to me\003, not \002explained me the concept\003. PHRASAL VERBS, IDIOMS & VOCABULARY Q44 - B. \002Carry out\003 means to perform or execute a task. Q45 - B. It refers to something initially negative that later proves helpful. Q46 - B. \002Diligent\003 means hardworking and careful. Q47 - C. \002Abundant\003 is the opposite of scarce. FIGURES OF SPEECH Q48 - B. The wind is given a human action: whispering. Q49 - A. The smile is directly compared to sunshine without \002like\003 or \002as\003. Q50 - B. The classroom is directly described as a zoo to suggest extreme disorder.
